People of Willowshore

For over a century, the souls of the slain townspeople repeated the same year in a mindscape that annually loops time back on itself. As far as these residents—including the PCs—are concerned, this adventure begins at the onset of summer in 7108, a mere two years after the fall of Lung Wa. Current trending topics are the recent exodus of the lumber lords, news of the jorogumo seizing control of the nation, and preparations for the upcoming season of ghosts.

Willowshore’s Name

The people of Willowshore come from a wide range of cultures and nations, and as such, the inspirations for the NPCs, legends, and lore of the town are inspired by a widespread number of real-world Asian sources. While individual NPCs found in Willowshore might have naming conventions inspired by real-world Asian countries, the name of the town itself is presented as a compound word in English. This is a deliberate attempt to capture the feel of a place that belongs to a wide range of Asian cultures but isn’t dominated by one.

Many Willowshorers identify by when their family first settled in town, which often affects which bank of the Ceiba River they live on. The first wave of townspeople are either those who worked on the monastery or who were paid to settle in Willowshore by the monastery. These folks originally lived south of the river and are thus referred to as Southbankers. Those who arrived after Lung Wa took control, meanwhile, settled on the river’s northern banks, called Northridge due to its prominent incline. These settlers included workers for the lumber bosses, businesses that wanted convenient access to the lumber, and imperial guards.

Though these two factions in Willowshore today use the names Southbank and Northridge, one’s allegiance isn’t solely determined by where they live or work. Southbank folks are traditionalists, keen on maintaining Willowshore’s culture and living simply off the land. Northridge folks, meanwhile, focus on modern pragmatism and urban growth. Many Northridge folks are open to the idea of jorogumo ruling Shenmen, while Southbankers on principle think jorogumo are evil monsters and best avoided.

Despite disagreements, both sides have a consensus on putting Willowshore’s survival and safety first. Plenty of residents have their own opinions that lean in neither direction and consider themselves unaffiliated with either faction. Overall, Willowshore values giving all one has to offer. In many ways, the village has no choice, especially as the events of this adventure evolve.

The following stat block presents the town of Willowshore as it stands at the start of this campaign. As the Adventure Path continues, Willowshore’s level will grow as a result of the PCs’ work fighting against the sinister forces plaguing the region—see the “Growing the Town” sidebar for more details.

Note that the population figure in the Willowshore stat block accounts for the town’s population after the PCs finish @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog04reclai]{Chapter 2} and things finally start to “get back to normal.” Feel free to increase this population total slightly if your PCs manage to save an unexpected number of locals from death during @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog03toligh]{Chapter 1} and 2, but the dead bodies and victims the PCs encounter during those first two chapters are poor souls who are not included in these totals. If this weren’t destined to be the final cycle the mindscape endures (either because Kugaptee emerges into the real world and consumes it all, or because the PCs manage to stop the fiend and return Willowshore to reality), these victims would return to life in a year.

Growing the Town

As of the start of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog05thewil]{Chapter 3}, Willowshore is a 4th-level settlement that has just endured a brutal monster attack. Helping the townspeople recover and getting Willowshore back “on its feet” is a recurring theme throughout this campaign. As the PCs accomplish milestone events, as detailed in each act, they effectively increase Willowshore’s level. While this doesn’t impact the town’s population total, it does increase the baseline for what items can be purchased in town and the baseline maximum for most task levels for Earning Income in town. Willowshore’s NPCs also grow in power as the PCs help build morale and reestablish themselves. Increase all NPC DCs and skill modifiers in Willowshore by 1 each time Willowshore gains a level above 4. Additionally, the level of each location increases by 1 each time Willowshore increases a level, which allows the PCs to take higher-level tasks when Earning Income.

Willowshore won’t gain levels as fast as the PCs. The town’s periodic level increases are less about the town itself growing in size and more about the PCs restoring morale and helping locals recover from recent events to bring Willowshore back to its previous height, before everything went bad.

The Willowshore Mindscape.name: 柳岸镇的思维空间 The Willowshore Mindscape
The Willowshore Mindscape.text:
柳岸镇的思维空间

对于那些被困在心景中的人来说，这里与现实世界毫无区别。魔法如人们所预期的那样运作，而从其他位面召来的生物也会以为自己是被召唤到了凡人世界。任何信息上的出入，例如如今是哪一年、发生过哪些事件，都很容易因柳岸镇地处偏远而被搪塞过去。尽管柳岸镇的人民在现实世界中于7108年遭到杀害，但他们在柳岸镇心景之中依然实实在在地活着。最终，环绕这片区域的超自然边界总会被发现，迫使柳岸镇的人民接受自己如今这种不自然的新处境；但每年春季的最后一天，时间都会重置，所有关于理解心景本质的记忆与进展也都会一并归零，循环再次开始。这样的情况已经持续了115年。

柳岸腹地 心景

  • 有限
  • 循环时间

柳岸镇心景是一个拟真思维空间，详见《开拓者：黑暗档案》第199页，但你在主持《肆季鬼志》时并不需要查阅那本书。思维空间的居民，包括玩家角色在内，在这条冒险路径后续阶段之前都不会意识到自身的真实处境。

柳岸镇心景具有循环时间特征，并被锁定在一个“时间回路”之中。这个心景有一个固定的时间起点，并在一年流逝后抵达终点。当时间来到这一年一度的终点时，心景中的一切（包括所有心景原生居民）都会在时间上回退。前一年的所有发展、成就与记忆都会失去，一切都重置回最初开始时的状态。这会让所有原生生物恢复到先前的年龄，将他们的生命值与所在位置重置到起始时的状态，甚至连在过去一年中死去者也会被复活术。循环心景原生者一旦死亡，其灵魂不会进入灵魂之河，而是会停滞不动，等待心景当前循环结束。在某些情况下，过往循环那些诡异的回响会以奇特而独一无二的方式累积，进而形成类似作祟的显现或不死生物，例如 @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia.JournalEntryPage.21thatchling0000]{草人}。

在每一次循环期间，事件都会以完全相同的方式推进，除非某种外来影响（例如来自另一现实的来访生物）打乱这些事件，从而可能在该次循环剩余时间里造成截然不同的局面。当循环心景重置时，外来的物体或访客会被保留下来，他们对于先前循环的记忆也同样会保留，并可随其所愿利用这些记忆为自己谋利。这样的事在柳岸镇心景中以前从未发生过，但这一次，情况将会不同。

思维空间的居民

柳岸镇中居住着四类居民。

被困住的灵魂：柳岸镇的居民（包括玩家角色），以及腹地中大多数有智慧的生物，都在7108年死去，随后被困在心景中，以活着的状态存在，且没有自己死亡的记忆。

非智慧生物：像动物伙伴或魔宠这类生物在灵性上与玩家角色相连，因此被视作被困住的灵魂；但栖居于心景中的其余非智慧野生动物与植物生命则如其种类对应的普通动物般正常活动，却不具备任何类似灵魂的东西——它们被杀死后会像往常一样腐朽，但无法变成不死生物，也无法恢复生命。

怪物化身：邪魔苦迦菩提的影响带来了具备实体与自由意志的怪物显现，这些怪物在心景上一个循环终结时出现，并持续到了这一个循环中。它们并没有关于心景形成之前自身存在的真实记忆，也不具备灵魂，但除此之外，它们在其他方面都如同其种类的普通怪物一般运作。它们既不能被带回生命，也不能变成不死生物，但它们死后尸体仍会留下，并像平常一样腐朽。

访客：心景中有极少数居民是来自边界之外的访客。名为信藏的死神商人便是其中一例，玩家角色从第二幕开始将遭遇到的灵堕魔也是如此。

The Willowshore Mindscape

For those trapped within the mindscape, it’s indistinguishable from the living world. Magic functions as one expects, and creatures conjured from other planes assume they’ve been called into the mortal realm. Any discrepancy in information, such as what year it is and what events took place, can easily be dismissed due to Willowshore’s remoteness. While the people of Willowshore were slain in the real world in 7108, they remain very much alive within Willowshore’s mindscape. Inevitably, the supernatural borders that surround the region are discovered, forcing the citizens of Willowshore to come to terms with their new unnatural situation, but every year on the last day of spring, time resets and all memory and progress toward understanding the nature of the mindscape resets, starting the cycle over again. And so it has been for 115 years.

Willowshore Hinterlands Mindscape

  • Finite
  • Cyclic Time

The Willowshore mindscape is an immersive mindscape, as detailed on page 199 of Pathfinder Dark Archives, but you won’t need to reference that book to run Season of Ghosts. The mindscape’s inhabitants, including the PCs, remain unaware of their reality until later in the Adventure Path.

Willowshore’s mindscape has the cyclic time trait and is locked into a “time loop.” The mindscape has a set point in time when it starts and when it ends after the passage of a year. When time reaches this yearly end point, everything within the mindscape (including all natives of the mindscape) revert in time. All developments, accomplishments, and memories of the previous year are lost, and everything resets to the state things were at the start. This restores all native creatures to their previous age, resets their health and location to where they were at the start, and even resurrects those who died during the past year. The soul of a cyclic mindscape native who dies doesn’t enter the River of Souls but instead remains in stasis awaiting the end of the mindscape’s current cycle. In some cases, eerie echoes of previous cycles can accumulate in strange and unique ways, resulting in haunt-like manifestations or undead creatures, such as @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia.JournalEntryPage.21thatchling0000]{Thatchlings}.

During each cycle, events proceed identically unless an outside influence (such as a visiting creature from another reality) disrupts these events, potentially setting up a significantly different scenario for the rest of that cycle’s remaining time. When a cyclic mindscape resets, foreign objects or visitors remain, along with their memories of previous cycles, and they can use these memories to their advantage as they see fit. Such events have never happened in Willowshore’s mindscape before, but this time, things will be different.

Mindscape Inhabitants

Four types of inhabitants dwell in Willowshore.

Trapped Souls: The citizens of Willowshore (including the PCs), as well as most of the sapient creatures in the hinterlands, perished in 7108 and then became trapped, alive and with no memories of their deaths, in the mindscape.

Non-Sapient Creatures: Creatures like animal companions or familiars are linked spiritually to PCs and are considered to be trapped souls, but the rest of the non-sapient wildlife and plant life that dwells in the mindscape function as normal animals of their kind but lack anything akin to a soul—when they’re slain, they decay as normal but can’t become undead, nor can they be restored to life.

Monstrous Manifestations: The influence of the fiend Kugaptee introduces physical and free-willed manifestations of monsters whose appearance at the end of the mindscape’s previous cycle have persisted into this one. They have no true memories of their existence before the mindscape’s formation, nor do they possess a soul, but they otherwise function as typical monsters of their kind. They can’t be brought back to life or become undead, but their bodies remain after death and decay as normal.

Visitors: A very few inhabitants of the mindscape are visitors from beyond its border. The shinigami merchant named Shinzo is one example here, as are nindoru fiends the PCs will encounter starting in the second act.

Willowshore.name: 柳岸镇 Willowshore
Willowshore.text:
柳岸镇

柳岸镇的建立深受@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog18sangpo]{桑博齐}苦修传统的影响。帝国纪年6223年，谭隋靖以凯旋般的自我牺牲之举击败邪魔苦迦菩提之后，桑博齐修行者之间兴起了一项挑战，要去定位穗静所化作的那棵杉树。到了7020年，一位水名法号为@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia.JournalEntryPage.21zhihui00000000]{智惠}大师的桑博齐宗师完成了这一壮举。为了确保其他人也能亲自安全前往那棵树所在的林地，智惠大师决定将这棵杉树供奉于丹杉寺中，好让桑博齐修行者能够前来体悟这一哲学。

场景注释氛围 / Macro

@UUID[Playlist.HgqDtdyAVJFT3Dr1.PlaylistSound.x5igH32eFlcD1P5V]{柳岸镇} | @UUID[Macro.qMjiMOWIstGMjrXk]{更换季节}

当地多林且属山地地形，这让建设工作异常艰难，即便对最老练的建造者也是如此。有些人拒绝在那里休息，因为在曾有人死去的地方附近睡觉——哪怕那是出于高尚的原因——也是一种禁忌。智惠大师欣然为这些工人提供便利，并设法筹措资金，在山脚下为他们修建宿舍和其他设施；物资会被运送到河畔一处便利的港口卸下。负责摆渡运送物资的商人开始把这个偏远聚落称作“柳树盈岸”，这是当地一句意为“根本找不到”的比喻。久而久之，这个名字就与聚落联系在了一起，并缩略成了柳岸镇。

寺院历经五年艰苦建设后，工人们将重心转向扩建柳岸镇，兴建客栈、农舍和其他建筑，以支撑越来越多长期访客的需求。在寺院最鼎盛的时期，几乎每一家商店或农庄都会为朝圣者提供餐食和床位。随着智惠大师于7054年去世，这股经济繁荣也逐渐消退；丹杉寺开始缓慢衰落时，许多柳岸镇居民也开始到更远的地方施展自己的技能、贩售货物以维持生计。

7060年，神门征召这座村庄，使其成为龙华采伐木材宏图的一部分。起初一切进展顺利，还修建了包括桥梁和水坝在内的基础设施。然而，负责采伐作业的木材老板很快因剥削柳岸镇苦修历史而遭人憎恨。更糟的是，他们开始把这处定居点——如今已正式称为城镇——包装成供龙华贵族消遣的“度假胜地”，让这些人前来游猎取乐，并享用那些以帝皇之名强行征收来的食物与酒水。

木材老板和政府对那座早已废弃的寺院几乎毫不关心，直到他们贪婪扩张的脚步于7062年伸向谭杉林，而一次采伐圣树的企图最终以血腥屠杀收场。唯一幸存者的证词，让废弃寺院在柳岸镇内彻底坐实了恶名。此后数周乃至数月间，怪物目击事件日益增多，受任命的总督则以土地或财产作为补偿承诺，吸引帝皇军队进驻城镇，以换取他们所能提供的防护。最终，这些士兵中有许多人在当地退役，成为镇中新一波定居者。

7106年龙华崩溃时，柳岸镇的木材领主们带着自己的财富，抛下庄园逃之夭夭。大多数士兵返回了神门的首都，或干脆弃守岗位，只留下那些已经在当地扎下根的人。尽管柳岸镇地处偏远，使它免于猖獗的匪患与外部政治冲突之害，但这种孤立也让重大消息传来得更晚。直到7108年晚春，柳岸镇才得知络新妇接管整个神门的消息；这一消息迫使镇上的总督赫山宝尝试举行一场危险的仪式，想要恢复丹杉寺的防护力量。然而这场仪式适得其反，反而唤醒了邪魔苦迦菩提留下的遗祸，最终造成了一股毁灭性的力量浪潮，悲惨地杀死了全镇所有人。

次日，太阳照耀在一座已无生命的柳岸镇上；而对外部世界而言，这座城镇在此后一百多年里始终只是个废弃的鬼故事源头。然而，在这场事件中死去的人从未意识到自己的命运，因为他们被杀的灵魂被困在了一个平行现实之中。他们滞留在生死之间这一片奇异的边 limbo 中，栖居于一处心景里；对于生活在其领域中的人而言，那地方与现实几乎没有区别。

Willowshore

Willowshore’s founding is steeped in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog18sangpo]{Sangpotshi} asceticism. After Tan Sui-Jing’s triumphant act of self-sacrifice defeated the fiend Kugaptee in 6223 ic, there rose a challenge among Sangpotshi practitioners to locate the sugi tree Sui-Jing transformed into. In 7020, a Sangpotshi master under the Fluvial name of Master @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia.JournalEntryPage.21zhihui00000000]{Zhi Hui} accomplished this feat. To ensure that others could safely visit the tree’s grove themselves, Master Zhi Hui decided to enshrine the sugi within the Tan Sugi monastery, where Sangpotshi practitioners could come to reflect upon the philosophy.

Scene NotesAmbiance / Macro

@UUID[Playlist.HgqDtdyAVJFT3Dr1.PlaylistSound.x5igH32eFlcD1P5V]{Willowshore} | @UUID[Macro.qMjiMOWIstGMjrXk]{Change Season}

The wooded and mountainous terrain made construction immensely difficult, even for the most seasoned of builders. Some refused to rest there, as the idea of sleeping near a place where another died (even for a noble cause) was taboo. Master Zhi Hui gladly accommodated these workers and sought funds to build them living quarters and other facilities at the foot of the mountain where supplies were dropped off at a convenient harbor along the riverside. The merchants ferrying in the supplies took to calling the remote settlement “the shore of willows,” a local metaphor meaning “impossible to find.” In time, the name became associated with the settlement, shortened to Willowshore.

After five years of hard work on the monastery, the workers turned their focus to expanding Willowshore, building inns, farmhouses, and other structures to support a growing stream of long-term visitors. At the height of the monastery’s popularity, almost every shop or farm offered a meal and bed for pilgrims. This economic boom faded with Master Zhi Hui’s death in 7054, and many Willowshore residents began to ply their skills and wares further afield to earn a living as the Tan Sugi monastery began its slow decline.

In 7060, Shenmen enlisted the village to become part of Lung Wa’s lumber harvesting ambitions. Things started out well, with the construction of infrastructure, including bridges and a dam. However, the lumber bosses who ran the harvesting operation soon became loathed for their exploitation of Willowshore’s ascetic past. Worse, they began to present the settlement (now properly called a town) as a “getaway” for Lung Wa aristocrats to hunt for sport and indulge in food and drinks forcefully seized in the empire’s name.

The lumber bosses and government cared little for the long-abandoned monastery until their greedy expansion reached for the Tan Sugi grove in 7062 and an attempt to harvest the sacred trees ended in grisly slaughter. The sole survivor’s testimony cemented an ill reputation within Willowshore of the abandoned monastery. As monster sightings grew in the weeks and months after, the appointed governor responded by enticing imperial forces to move into the town with the promise of land or property in compensation for the protection they could offer. Many of these soldiers would ultimately retire in the region, becoming a new wave of settlers in the town.

When Lung Wa collapsed in 7106, Willowshore’s lumber lords took their wealth, abandoned their estates, and fled. Most soldiers returned to Shenmen’s capital or deserted their posts, leaving behind those who had put down local roots. Though Willowshore’s remoteness saved it from the rampant banditry and external political conflicts, the isolation also delayed major news. Willowshore didn’t learn of the jorogumo takeover of all Shenmen until late spring of 7108, news that compelled the town’s governor, Heh Shan-Bao, to attempt a dangerous ritual to restore the protective power of the Tan Sugi monastery. The ritual backfired and instead awakened the fiend Kugaptee’s legacy, resulting in a devastating wave of power that tragically killed the entire town.

The sun rose the next day on a Willowshore devoid of life, and to the world at large, the town has remained an abandoned source of ghost stories for over a hundred years. However, those who perished in this event never realized their fate, for their slain souls became trapped in an alternate reality. Stuck in a strange limbo between life and death, they reside in a mindscape largely indistinguishable from reality to those who live within its realm.

Act 1.1: To Light the Night.name: 第一幕 1.1：点亮长夜 Act 1.1: To Light the Night

Light the Night.name: 点亮夜晚 Light the Night
Light the Night.text:
点亮夜晚

长明灯是一件位于晨步桥南侧、无法移动的15级魔法物品。这盏石制提灯是一座5英尺高的石灯，由产自薄纱群山、夹杂银纹的花岗岩雕成。其内部有一个冷铁笼子，笼中有一座莲花形底座，底座上曾摆放着三枚发光的铜币。据说，这盏灯发出的光能够保护柳岸镇免受各种邪恶侵害。多年前，智惠大师将其赠予柳岸镇；自镇上任何人有记忆以来，这盏提灯从未熄灭。然而当怪物入侵城镇时，独眼怪咕噜肚发现了这些发光的铜币并一把抢走，却在把它们从碗中取出后，发现这些“魔法”铜币立刻失去光芒，不禁大失所望。

要重新点亮这盏提灯，所有玩家角色需要做的只是打开长明灯南面的格栅，将三枚受祝福的铜币放进里面的冷铁笼子中，然后再将格栅关上。上述每一步都是一个单独的交互动作，而当最后一步完成时，提灯便会再次点燃。当长明灯点亮且三枚铜币仍留在内部时，它会在30英尺半径内提供光照（接下来的30英尺则为昏暗光照）；但更重要的是，点亮它会使笼罩柳岸镇的蜃景雾、绯红之月与血雨效果立刻终止。任何曾被赋予残酷知性与说话能力的动物，也都会恢复成普通动物，并自行离开城镇。

场景注记宏

@UUID[Macro.8KtgPGYgJdlDgXwI]{光明 长明灯}

每当玩家角色将柳岸镇各处圣祠相关的神圣祝福用于提灯时，这些力量背后的诸位神祇都会注意到，而祂们的关注与认可，会在提灯之光重新绽放的瞬间赐予玩家角色一项恩赐。这项恩赐使玩家角色在进行与该神祇神圣技能相关的技能检定时获得+1物品加值。举例来说，若玩家角色放入的是由@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.AlL9GtlTldbqNoVm]{卡莉丝翠雅}、@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.JgqH3BhuEuA4Zyqs]{黛丝娜}与@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.s9opv94lGDRKnw6W]{诗孜璐}祝福过的铜币，他们将分别在欺瞒、特技与社群检定上获得+1物品加值。由于这些全都是物品加值，因此使用同一座圣祠的多枚受祝福铜币，或使用来自拥有相同神圣技能之神祇的铜币，都不会带来额外优势。同样地，玩家角色最终也可能发现，他们在战役其余期间获得的魔法物品，可能会提供比这些恩赐更高的物品加值。无论是谁放入铜币，每位玩家角色都会获得这些恩赐的效果，因为神祇知晓玩家角色正在通力合作，也明白能够拯救或毁灭柳岸镇的，正是他们的命运。

奖励：玩家角色第一次点亮长明灯时，给予其80 XP。这也会提升玩家角色在镇上的声望。他们在第一次点亮提灯时，会分别在柳岸镇的两个派系中各获得1声望点。

Light the Night

The Eternal Lantern is an immobile 15th-level magical item located on the southern side of Dawnstep Bridge. This stone lantern is a 5-foot-tall stone lamp carved from silver-laced granite from the Gossamer Mountains. Its interior contains a cold iron cage with a lotus-shaped pedestal on which three glowing copper coins once sat. It’s said that the light from this lamp protects Willowshore from all manners of evil. Gifted to Willowshore many years ago by Master @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia.JournalEntryPage.21zhihui00000000]{Zhi Hui}, the lantern has never been extinguished for as long as anyone in town can remember, but when the monsters invaded the town, the buso Gurglegut spotted the glowing coins and snatched them up, only to be disappointed when the “magic” coins went dark after he took them from the bowl.

To relight the lantern, all the PCs need to do is open the grill on the Eternal Lantern’s southern face, place three blessed copper coins in the cold iron cage within, and then close the grill. Each of these is a single Interact action, and once the last is completed, the lantern ignites once more. While the Eternal Lantern is lit and the three coins remain inside, it sheds light in a 30-foot radius (and dim light for the next 30 feet), but more importantly, lighting it causes the mirage mist, crimson moon, and blood rain effects that have settled over Willowshore to immediately end. Any animals that had been granted cruel sapience and the ability to speak revert to normal animals as well and make their way back out of town.

Scene NotesMacro

@UUID[Macro.8KtgPGYgJdlDgXwI]{Light Eternal Lantern}

The various divine forces associated with Willowshore’s shrines take note whenever their blessings are used in the lantern by the PCs, and their interest and approval results in a boon granted to the PCs as soon as the lantern’s light shines out. This boon grants the PCs a +1 item bonus to skill checks they attempt with the deity’s divine skill. For example, if the PCs place coins blessed by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.AlL9GtlTldbqNoVm]{Calistria}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.JgqH3BhuEuA4Zyqs]{Desna}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.s9opv94lGDRKnw6W]{Shizuru}, they’ll receive a +1 item bonus to Deception, Acrobatics, and Society respectively. Since these are all item bonuses, there’s no advantage to using multiple blessed coins from the same shrine or from deities who share the same divine skill. Likewise, the PCs might eventually find that magic items they gain during the rest of the campaign could provide greater item bonuses than those granted by these boons. Each PC gains the effects of these boons, regardless of who placed the coins, as the gods know the PCs are working together, and that it’s their destiny that can save or damn Willowshore.

Reward: Grant the PCs 80 XP the first time they light the Eternal Lantern. This also increases the PCs’ reputation in town. They gain 1 Reputation Point with both of Willowshore’s factions the first time they light the lantern.

Retaking Dawnstep.name: 重夺黎明阶梯 Retaking Dawnstep
Retaking Dawnstep.text:
重夺黎明阶梯 中等 1

本次遭遇使用晨步桥的地图。

生物：坐在晨步桥上临时王座里的那个大型身影，是一只名叫辘肠的蹒跚独眼怪；而周围较小的一群，则是几只蹑影小魔怪，正竭尽所能取悦他们暴力的首领。对玩家角色来说，幸运的是，他们不需要同时和所有这些怪物作战——任何接近桥梁的举动都会很快吸引它们的注意，但只有辘肠会走上前，在桥的南端拦住玩家角色。蹑影小魔怪们会留在后面讥笑并嘲弄玩家角色，但只要有任何真正针对它们的攻击，小魔怪们就会尖叫着惊慌逃走。

如果玩家角色带着一份下了毒的酒作为礼物接近，辘肠会开心大笑，迅速一把夺过礼物喝下，然后挥手赶走玩家角色。如果他因这酒而失去意识，蹑影小魔怪们会以为他死了，惊慌逃跑；但如果在他仍然清醒时，玩家角色再次靠近（或者一开始就拒绝离开），他就会立刻发动攻击。

重夺黎明阶梯 中等 1

@UUID[Actor.EFX5AOuSEa0cxcj1]{辘肠}

辘肠醉得厉害，因此在本次遭遇中实际上处于 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{恶心 2}。他在战斗开始时会先用第一个动作尝试进行一次 @Check[fortitude|dc:15] 强韧豁免，以减少自己的恶心值；接着用第二个动作尝试对看起来最难对付的玩家角色施展挫败士气。第三个动作要么是行走到那个玩家角色身边，要么是用他的廓尔喀弯刀打击一个邻近角色。在之后的每一轮开始时，他都会先花一个动作尝试减轻自己的恶心状态，直到完全恢复。不管怎样，他都会战斗至死。

宝藏： @UUID[Actor.GQ5mt29CNdfsJZyz]{辘肠的宝藏}
辘肠收集了几件宝藏，就放在他临时王座附近——一根价值 15 gp 的镶嵌半宝石的银权杖，以及一个价值 5 gp 的精致的银制珠宝盒，盒中装着一枚谨慎戒指。此外，这只独眼怪还在口袋里带着三枚古老的铜钱币——若角色成功通过一次 @Check[willowshore-lore|dc:15|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] 检定来回忆知识，便能正确辨认出这三枚钱币正是长久以来维持长明灯燃烧的那些钱币。这三枚钱币如今已不再带有祝福，其价值也仅止于此——3 cp。

奖励：如果玩家角色为柳岸镇除掉辘肠，从而重新打通晨步桥，他们将从每个派系各获得 1 点声望点。

Retaking Dawnstep Moderate 1

Use the map for Dawnstep Bridge for this encounter.

Creatures: The large figure seated on the improvised throne on Dawnstep Bridge is a lumbering buso named Gurglegut, while the smaller crowd are several jinkins who are doing their best to keep their violent leader entertained. Fortunately for the PCs, they don’t need to fight all of these monsters at once—any approach to the bridge quickly attracts their attention, but only Gurglegut steps forward to confront the PCs at the south end of the bridge. The jinkins hang back to jeer and taunt the PCs, but any actual attack directed toward them causes the gremlins to shriek and flee in panic.

If the PCs approach with a gift of poisoned wine, Gurglegut laughs in delight and quickly snatches up the gift and drinks it, waving the PCs away. If he falls unconscious from the drink, the jinkins panic and flee, thinking he died, but if the PCs approach again (or refuse to leave in the first place) while he’s still conscious, he attacks at once.

Retaking Dawnstep Moderate 1

@UUID[Actor.EFX5AOuSEa0cxcj1]{Gurglegut}

Gurglegut is drunk enough that he’s effectively @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} during this encounter. He opens the fight by spending his first action to attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:15] save to reduce his sickened value, then uses his second action to try to Demoralize the toughest-looking PC. His third action is either to Stride up to that PC or to Strike an adjacent character with his kukri. He starts each following round with an action to try to reduce his sickened condition until he’s fully recovered. In any event, he fights to the death.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.GQ5mt29CNdfsJZyz]{Gurglegut's Treasures}
Gurglegut has gathered a few treasures that he keeps near his impromptu throne—a silver scepter set with semi-precious stones worth 15 gp and an elegant silver jewelry case worth 5 gp that contains a ring of discretion. In addition, the buso carries three ancient copper coins in a pocket—a character who succeeds at a @Check[willowshore-lore|dc:15|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge correctly identifies these three coins as those that, for so long, kept the Eternal Lantern lit. These three coins no longer bear blessings and are worth precisely that—3 cp.

Reward: If the PCs rid Willowshore of Gurglegut and thus reopen Dawnstep Bridge, they earn 1 Reputation Point with each faction.

Liberating the Bridge.name: 解放桥梁 Liberating the Bridge
Liberating the Bridge.text:
解放桥梁

晨步桥（区域 @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog02willow.JournalEntryPage.02w11dawnstepb00]{W11}）是连接城镇两岸的重要通道，但如果玩家角色此时决定调查，他们会发现桥上有一只独眼怪和数只蹑影小魔怪把守。一旦玩家角色来到100英尺内，并且细节在雾气中或诡异的月光下变得可见，就朗读以下内容。

血迹涂抹在晨步桥的灰色石面上，证明这里最近发生过一场战斗。柳岸镇标志性的石制提灯火焰——有记忆以来第一次——熄灭了。一个高大的人形身影坐在由堆放在桥上的偷来家具组成的王座上。他一边从酿煮锅里喝着东西，一边看着周围几个小得多的人形生物蹦跳嬉闹，显然是在模仿并嘲弄近期受害者临死前的挣扎与反应。

玩家角色可以花一些时间观察这些怪物；它们喧闹嬉戏的声音大到足以让玩家角色在远处观看它们的滑稽举动，而无须掷隐秘检定。不过，他们仍需要尝试一次秘密 @Check[perception|dc:15|traits:secret] 检定，以便从10分钟的观察中捕捉线索。

大成功 玩家角色注意到，蹑影小魔怪会说通用语（这些小魔怪大多只是在滑稽地扮演惊惧的镇民），但那个更大的独眼身影并没有在留心。那大个子偶尔开口时，要么是醉醺醺地用妖精语哼唱几句关于酒精的蹩脚打油诗，要么是吹嘘自己如何以暴力战胜本地人。听上10分钟后，玩家角色得知了这支入侵势力中似乎三名首领的名字——辘肠、灰屠夫，以及莫斗秋——不过并没有迹象表明谁是谁，也不知道这三个生物究竟是什么。

成功 玩家角色得知，蹑影小魔怪与那个大个子身影似乎并不共享同一种语言。

失败 除了确认敌人的数量之外，玩家角色没有从观察中得到任何值得注意的信息。

大失败 玩家角色错误地得出结论，认为那个大个子身影已经快要昏过去了。

除了最初的10分钟外，玩家角色还可以继续尝试额外的 @Check[perception|dc:15|traits:secret] 检定，但每多观察10分钟，如果他们的隐秘检定未能成功以维持藏匿状态，这些怪物就有机会注意到玩家角色。如果玩家角色被发现，蹑影小魔怪会兴奋地尖叫，其中四只小魔怪会追上来。

与四只蹑影小魔怪的战斗属于一次1级极限遭遇——玩家角色最好选择逃跑。蹑影小魔怪会又叫又笑，追上几轮后便会心满意足地放弃，因为它们已经成功吓到了这些人类；但如果它们与玩家角色交战并击败了他们，那么在辘肠介入之前，这支队伍可能需要当地居民出手救援。

奖励： 因侦察这些怪物，给予玩家角色10 XP，并使他们在两个派系中各获得1点声望点。

Liberating the Bridge

Dawnstep Bridge (area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog02willow.JournalEntryPage.02w11dawnstepb00]{W11}) is an important link between the town’s two shores, but if the PCs decide to investigate at this time, they find the bridge guarded by a buso and several jinkins. Read the following once the PCs come within 100 feet and the details become visible through the mist or under the eerie moonlight.

Blood smears the gray stone of Dawnstep Bridge, evidence of a recent fight. The flame of Willowshore’s iconic stone lantern is—for the first time in memory—extinguished. A large humanoid figure sits on a throne made of stolen furniture heaped on the bridge. As he drinks from a brewing pot, several much smaller humanoids around him caper about, apparently mimicking and mocking death throes and reactions of recent victims.

The PCs can spend some time observing the monsters, who are cavorting loudly enough that the PCs can watch their antics from a distance without needing to roll Stealth checks. However, they do need to attempt a secret @Check[perception|dc:15|traits:secret] check to pick up on clues from 10 minutes of observation.

Critical Success The PC notes that the jinkins speak Common (the gremlins are mostly just play-acting roles of comically frightened townsfolk), but the larger, one-eyed figure isn’t paying attention. The few times the larger figure speaks, it’s to drunkenly sing out (in Fey) a few rhymes of bad poetry about alcohol or to boast of his violent triumphs against the locals. After listening for 10 minutes, the PC learns the names of what appear to be the three ringleaders of the invading force—Gurglegut, Gray Butcher, and Mo Douqiu—although there’s no indication who’s who or what these three creatures are.

Success The PC learns that the jinkins and larger figure don’t seem to share a language.

Failure The PC learns nothing of note from their observations other than confirming numbers of foes.

Critical Failure The PC comes to the incorrect conclusion that the large figure is on the verge of passing out.

The PCs can attempt additional @Check[perception|dc:15|traits:secret] checks beyond the first 10 minutes, but each additional 10 minutes they do so, the monsters get a chance to notice the PCs if they don’t succeed at their Stealth checks to remain hidden. If the PCs are noticed, the jinkins shriek in excitement, and four of the gremlins give chase.

A fight against four jinkins is an Extreme 1 encounter—one from which the PCs would be wise to flee. The jinkins hoot and shriek and give up the chase after a few rounds, pleased to have scared the humans, but if they fight and defeat the PCs, the party might need to be rescued by locals before Gurglegut gets involved.

Reward: Grant the PCs 10 XP and 1 Reputation Point with both factions for spying on the monsters.

圣所位置

当玩家角色尝试进行一次关于地点的 @Check[willowshore-lore|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] 检定以回忆知识时，他们掷骰一次，并得知所有“发现”难度等级等于或低于其检定结果的圣祠位置。表格条目依“发现”难度等级数值从低到高排列，便于一眼看出角色发现了众多圣祠中的哪些。

The PCs can also learn of some of these more obscure shrine locations by exploring the town or by speaking to various NPCs. At your discretion, if a PC worships a deity or follows a faith not listed on the following table, they might have a small personal shrine to their faith set up in their own home.

When a PC attempts a @Check[willowshore-lore|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge about locations, they roll once and learn the locations of all shrines with a Discover DC equal to or less than the result of their check.
