Now that he has become a monster and is wracked with guilt for what he did to Willowshore, Shan-Bao can hardly bear to look at the princess’s likeness. His efforts to tear apart her portrait are rooted in such powerful emotion that they withstood the mansion’s restorative magic, but even in the worst of his rages, Shan-Bao couldn’t bear to damage the portrait’s face.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.QlxKiUt5eSXPms8k]{Ruined Frame}
The portrait scrap can be easily removed from the frame. It’s one of the key objects that can be used to free Shan-Bao; however, it has no power, and in its damaged state, it isn’t worth more than 5 gp.

Manor Entrance.name: 庄园入口 Manor Entrance
Manor Entrance.text:
C1. 庄园入口

一对石狮守在庄园入口两侧，双眼闪烁着猩红色的光芒。北面，纸拉门阻挡了通往庄园内庭院的视线。

这座残破庄园中其他地方完全不见踪影的这两尊石狮，在PC进入房间时似乎活了过来，抬起前爪致意，随后又回到原本的位置。石狮的举止流露出一种如释重负之感，仿佛赋予它们行动的精魂因这座宅邸在长期遭受荒废之后终于落入值得托付之人手中而感到欣慰——它们本身并没有危险。

当PC进入庄园时，除非他们屏住呼吸或试图潜行，否则区域 @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog15afiend.JournalEntryPage.15c3servantsqu00]{C3a} 中的僵尸仆役会自动察觉到他们的到来。这些僵尸仆役会放下手头的活计，前去“迎接”PC，详情见区域 @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog15afiend.JournalEntryPage.15c3servantsqu00]{C3}。

C1. Manor Entrance

A pair of stone lions flanks the manor’s entrance, their eyes shimmering with crimson light. To the north, sliding paper walls block the view into the manor’s inner courtyard.

Completely missing from the ruined manor, the two stone lions found here appear to animate as the PCs enter the room, raising their forepaws in salute before returning to their original positions. The lions’ manner suggests relief, as if whatever spirit animates them is glad to have the mansion in trustworthy hands after a long history of neglect—they aren’t dangerous in and of themselves.

When the PCs enter the manor, unless they’re holding their breath or attempting to be stealthy, the jiang-shi servants in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog15afiend.JournalEntryPage.15c3servantsqu00]{C3a} will automatically notice their entrance. The jiang-shi set aside their tasks to go “greet” the PCs as detailed in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog15afiend.JournalEntryPage.15c3servantsqu00]{C3}.

Manor Features.name: 庄园特性 Manor Features
Manor Features.text:
庄园特性

与本幕开始时不同，玩家角色现在可以毫无畏惧地接近修复后的庄园。虽然拥有獠牙与钥匙有助于揭开修复后的庄园的一些秘密，但玩家角色并不需要持有它也能进入庄园。玩家角色在庄园外花费1轮进行专注后，会自动发现自己可以转移“焦点”，以观察庄园在现代世界中实际存在的样貌（作为一片废墟），或观察它完整修复后的存在形态；但一旦玩家角色进入修复后的庄园，他们就无法再在这两种现实之间切换。若以成功的 @Check[arcana|dc:25|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] 或 @Check[occultism|dc:25|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] 检定来回忆知识，玩家角色便会确认，这座修复后的庄园是一种心景，柳岸镇的合法统治者可以随意进出。

如果玩家角色进行试验，他们会发现：当他们进出修复后的庄园时，任何与他们有接触的生物都能在现实世界与修复后的庄园心景之间旅行；但若没有这种接触，这类生物便无法进入庄园，或者如果被遗留在庄园内，也无法离开。@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia.JournalEntryPage.21hehshanbao0001]{赫山宝}正是通过这种方式安置了修复后的庄园的守护者。

在修复完整的状态下，很容易看出这座庄园显然以健壮的木材建成，并以彩绘与瓦片精美装饰，但所有繁复加工的银质饰件都已被剥去，原处只剩裸露的木头或石材。庄园内部的格纸墙上装饰着自然、狩猎与社交聚会的美丽图景。大量提灯让庄园内部笼罩在明亮而诡异的红光中——任何向这些提灯内部窥视的人，都会看到光源是一团翻涌扭动、发光的灵堕魔蝴蝶球体。

虽然修复后的庄园内部墙壁和窗户可以如常被强行打开，但外部的则不行。任何这样做的尝试，都只会让玩家角色进入现实世界中那座破败的庄园废墟。同样，任何试图从上方进入修复后的庄园庭院的行为，都会导致角色只是进入那座破败庄园。只有通过区域 @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog15afiend.JournalEntryPage.15c1manorentra00]{C1} 的庄园正门，玩家角色才能在修复后的庄园与现实世界之间进出。

Manor Features

Unlike at the start of this act, the PCs can approach the restored manor without fear. While having the Fang and Key will help unlock some of the restored manor’s mysteries, possession isn’t required for a PC to enter the manor. A PC who concentrates for a round while outside of the manor automatically finds that they can shift their “focus” to observe the manor as it actually exists in the modern world (as a ruin) or as it exists fully restored, but once a PC enters the restored manor, they can’t change between these realities. With a successful @Check[arcana|dc:25|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[occultism|dc:25|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge, a PC confirms that this restored manor is a form of mindscape, one that can be entered or exited at will by those who rightfully rule Willowshore.

If the PCs experiment, they’ll find that any creature they’re in contact with when they come or go from the restored manor can travel between the real world and the restored manor’s mindscape, but without this contact, such creatures can’t enter the manor or, if abandoned within the manor, can’t leave. It was via this method that @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia.JournalEntryPage.21hehshanbao0001]{Heh Shan-Bao} installed the restored manor’s guardians.

In its restored condition, it’s easy to see that the manor was clearly built from hearty woods and is beautifully adorned with paint and tiles, but all of the ornately worked silver accents have been stripped away, leaving bare wood or stone in their place. The latticed paper walls within the manor are decorated with beautiful images of nature, hunts, and social gatherings. Numerous lanterns keep the interiors brightly lit with eerie red light—anyone who peers within any of these lanterns sees that the source of light is a writhing sphere of glowing nindoru butterflies.

While the restored manor’s interior walls and windows can be forced open normally, the exterior ones can’t. Any attempt to do so only allows the PCs to enter the ruined real-world manor. Likewise, any attempt to enter the restored manor’s courtyard from above results in the character simply entering the ruined manor. Only by using the manor’s front doors at area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog15afiend.JournalEntryPage.15c1manorentra00]{C1} can a PC come or go from the restored manor to the real world.

The Restored Manor.name: 修复后的庄园 The Restored Manor
The Restored Manor.text:
修复后的庄园

一旦PC成为柳岸镇的管理者，他们就可以进入总督庄园一个由超自然力量修复的版本。镇上唯一还能看见这一变化的其他人，是PC们在春天时帮助推举为柳岸镇领袖的那位镇中长者；但即便如此，在PC正式成为管理者之前，那位镇中长者也不会看见修复后的庄园，因为在那之前，他们被任命为总督一职在现代并不正式。若PC没有主动展开调查，你可以让那位镇中长者带着关于庄园为何会重建的问题来找他们，以此推动他们去调查修复后的庄园。

这一切都是@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia.JournalEntryPage.21hehshanbao0001]{赫山宝}计划的一部分，目的是防止闯入者重新进入如今已腐化的柳岸镇心景——他在那里统治。通过限制这些现实之间的通行，他希望限制他人接近自己的许可，却没有预料到一只络新妇会如此急切地将PC提升到现代神门政府中具有合法领导权的职位上。

尽管獠牙与钥匙仍不过是一枚发光的职权徽记，但在修复后的庄园中，它会作为一把隐喻性的钥匙发挥作用，开启更深层的秘密——并最终帮助PC发现，他们曾栖身其中的柳岸镇心景依然存在，只是已经变得截然不同，也更加可怖。

The Restored Manor

Once the PCs are made stewards of Willowshore, they can enter a supernaturally restored version of the governor’s manor. The only other person in town capable of seeing this change is the town elder whom the PCs helped install as Willowshore’s leader back in the spring, but even then, that town elder won’t see the restored manor until the PCs are made stewards since, until that point, their appointment to the role of governor wasn’t official in the modern era. You can use the town elder to spur the PCs to investigate the restored manor if they don’t pursue an investigation on their own by having the elder approach them with questions about how the manor got rebuilt.

All of this is part of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia.JournalEntryPage.21hehshanbao0001]{Heh Shan-Bao}’s plan to prevent intruders from making their way back into the now-corrupted Willowshore mindscape where he rules. By restricting passage between these realities, he hoped to limit access to himself, not anticipating a jorogumo’s eagerness to elevate the PCs to positions of legal leadership in modern Shenmen’s government.

While the Fang and Key remains little more than a glowing badge of office, within the restored manor, it functions as a metaphorical key that can unlock further secrets—and eventually help the PCs discover that the Willowshore mindscape they once dwelt in still exists, albeit in a much changed and much more horrific manner.

A Fiend in Two Worlds.name: 两界邪魔 A Fiend in Two Worlds
A Fiend in Two Worlds.text:
第13章： 两界邪魔

如果玩家角色在事件7：最后的季节期间，向行道女问出了正确的问题，他们应该会意识到，这一连串谋杀案的凶手正是@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia.JournalEntryPage.21hehshanbao0001]{赫山宝}——或者至少，是某个戴着他面孔的生物。此外，幻象中提到的“唯有正统统治者方可持有通往我领域的钥匙！”这句话，意在揭示：一旦玩家角色成为管事（因此正式跻身于现代柳岸镇的“正统统治者”之列），他们就可以返回赫山宝的庄园，并使用獠牙与钥匙直接与他对质。

当然，玩家角色也可能通过其他调查得出赫山宝就是凶手的结论；但如果他们迟迟无法理清他与案件的关系，你可以让任美璃提出这种可能性。如果玩家角色告诉她，行道女让他们在镜中看见了那段幻象，任美璃可以作出如下推测：“既然我已经让你们成为正统统治者了，也许现在正是时候再去看看你们前任总督的庄园？”

只要任何一名如今已是柳岸镇管事的玩家角色接近那片断壁残垣、也就是总督庄园的废墟30尺以内，处于范围内的这些玩家角色就会目睹令人震惊的一幕。对他们而言，而且只要他们始终停留在庄园围墙30尺范围内，这座建筑看起来便是完好如初的。屋檐下悬挂着提灯，散发出令人不安的红光，窗内也透出更多红色光芒。庄园仿佛已经恢复原状，但玩家角色注视得越久，心中就越发不安。

Chapter 13: A Fiend in Two Worlds

If the PCs asked the right question of the path maiden during Event 7: The Final Season, they should realize that the perpetrator of the murders is @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia.JournalEntryPage.21hehshanbao0001]{Heh Shan-Bao}—or some creature wearing his face, at the very least. Furthermore, the vision’s reference that “only a rightful ruler shall carry the key to my domain!” is meant to reveal that once the PCs become stewards (and thus are officially among the “rightful rulers” of modern Willowshore), they can return to Heh Shan-Bao’s manor and use the Fang and Key to confront him directly.

The PCs might have come to the conclusion that Heh Shan-Bao is the murderer through other investigations, of course, but if they’re struggling to figure out his involvement, you can have Ren Mei Li suggest the possibility. If the PCs tell her of the vision in the mirror granted by the path maiden, Ren Mei Li can make the following observation: “Now that I’ve made you rightful rulers, perhaps it’s time to revisit your ex-governor’s manor?”

As soon as any of the PCs, now stewards of Willowshore, approach within 30 feet of the dilapidated ruins that are the governor’s manor, those PCs in range witness something astounding. To them, and as long as they remain within 30 feet of the manor’s walls, the structure appears fully restored. Lanterns lit by an unsettling red light hang from the eaves, and additional red light glows from within its windows. The manor seems to be restored, but the longer a PC looks, the more unsettled they feel.

Continuing the Campaign.name: 延续战役 Continuing the Campaign

Into Kugaptee’s Mind.name: 进入苦迦菩提的心景 Into Kugaptee’s Mind
Into Kugaptee’s Mind.text:
进入苦迦菩提的心景

PC们必须决定，是将苦迦菩提之墓留给后世处理，还是冒险与宁多鲁展开最后一次正面决战。若他们选择后者，就必须前往天京的森杭寺院——三傀会的所在地，而赫山宝曾试图招募他们。

在天京，PC们发现自己被卷入当地的种种阴谋之中。尤其是布拉阔——一类四处游历、以10年任期担任信仰守护者的圣职者——会试图招募PC们，以增加他们关于乡野各地危险四起的报告分量。天京偏远边境长期遭受古魔攻击，这些古魔试图突破这个国家众多神圣封印，但位于首都、执政的年仁议会却始终低估这一威胁。

无论PC们是否协助布拉阔，他们最终都会前往偏远多山的森杭寺院，并发现那里也已遭到古魔渗透。整座寺院已被古魔彻底吞噬，只剩下少数长着人脸的同谋者阻挠外人查探。

如果PC们曾在布拉阔中结交盟友，他们在击败古魔时或许能获得宝贵的见解与工具。否则，PC们就只能独自杀穿这些腐化的废墟，在其中找到三傀会最后幸存者在死前设法保护下来的遗物。其中一些守护者是守护精魂，或是涂抹了圣油、以防古魔腐蚀的发条自动机；若它们相信这些闯入者值得协助，便可能出手相助。

在寺院废墟中，PC们可以取回天妙圣锣、数瓶发光的天火墨，以及能帮助他们对抗苦迦菩提的祝圣物品。天火墨可用于在进入宁多鲁那虽已死亡却仍在做梦的心景之前，将祷文涂写在自己身上；也可用来在丝带上绘制神圣印记，再将其系在额头上，以保护自己免受苦迦菩提心景构造物的侵害。击败宁多鲁时，必须敲响天妙圣锣，以确保天庭得知他的陨灭，并立刻将其灵魂拘往死后世界。

PC们进入苦迦菩提那被死亡笼罩的心景的方法，应当建立在他们于肆季鬼志期间已经学会的诸多仪式之上。当他们终于进入宁多鲁内化的心景时，映入眼帘的是一座令人痛苦的迷宫。重力与逻辑毫无意义；超现实的物体与狰狞的面孔漂浮在无尽虚空中；生者与死者彼此难分。PC们不仅必须在这些扭曲而荒谬的走廊中找到出路，还必须击败苦迦菩提凭意志创造出来、并以被吞噬灵魂碎片驱动的各种怪物。若没有从三傀会获得的工具，他们必定会迷失其中。

到了最后，PC们将与宁多鲁本人面对面：一个近乎神祇的存在，因这些一再阻挠他的英雄而被仇恨彻底吞噬。这场高潮之战理应足以流传千古；而在战斗结束后，PC们要么可以安心确信自己已经消除了天夏的一大严重威胁……要么就此沦为一位邪魔之神永世囚禁的玩物。

Into Kugaptee’s Mind

The PCs must decide whether to leave Kugaptee’s grave alone for future generations to handle or risk a final, direct confrontation with the nindoru. Should they choose the latter, they must visit the Senhang Monastery in Tianjing, home of the Fellowship of Sankuei, whom Heh Shan-Bao attempted to enlist.

In Tianjing, the PCs find themselves embroiled in local intrigues. In particular, the bulakho, a class of wandering holy people serving 10-year terms as defenders of the faith, try to enlist the PCs to add gravity to their reports of dangers arising across the countryside. The remote borders of Tianjing have faced continuous attacks from qlippoth trying to break through the nation’s many holy seals, but the ruling Nyenreng Conclave in the capital has consistently discounted the threat.

Whether or not the PCs aid the bulakho, they’ll eventually travel to the remote, mountainous Senhang Monastery and discover that it, too, has succumbed to qlippoth infiltration. The monastery has been entirely consumed by qlippoth, with just a few human-faced conspirators discouraging scrutiny from outsiders.

If the PCs have made allies among the bulakho, they might gain valuable insights and tools in defeating the qlippoth. Otherwise, the PCs are on their own in fighting their way through the corrupted ruins, where they can find relics that the last survivors of the Fellowship of Sankuei managed to safeguard before perishing. Some of these guardians are protective spirits or clockwork automatons smeared with holy unguents to protect them from qlippoth corrosion, and they might assist the PCs if they believe the interlopers to be worthy.

In the monastery’s ruins, the PCs can retrieve the Sacred Gong of Temyo, bottles of luminous skyfire ink, and blessed items that will aid them against Kugaptee. The skyfire ink can be used to cover themselves with prayers before entering the nindoru’s dead but dreaming mind, as well as to paint holy sigils onto silken bands they can bind about their brows to protect themselves from Kugaptee’s mindscape constructs. The Sacred Gong of Temyo must be sounded when the nindoru is defeated, to ensure that the Heavenly Court hears of his demise and seizes his soul for the afterworld at once.

The method by which the PCs enter Kugaptee’s death-shrouded mindscape should require them to build upon the many rituals they already learned during Season of Ghosts. When they finally enter the nindoru’s internalized mindscape, the PCs find themselves in a torturous labyrinth. Gravity and logic are meaningless; surreal objects and grotesque faces float in an infinite void; the living and unliving are indistinguishable from one another. Not only must the PCs navigate through the twisting, nonsensical corridors, they must also defeat the various monstrosities that Kugaptee has willed into existence and animated with fragments of devoured souls. Without the tools gained from the Fellowship of Sankuei, they’ll surely be lost.

At the end of it all, the PCs come face-to-face with the nindoru himself: a near-godlike entity consumed with hatred for the heroes who have denied him so much. The climactic fight should be one for the ages, but at the end of it, the PCs can rest confident that they have eliminated a grave threat to Tian Xia... or else consigned themselves to an eternity imprisoned as a fiend-god’s playthings.

The Ghostly Governor.name: 幽灵总督 The Ghostly Governor
The Ghostly Governor.text:
幽灵总督

威胁柳岸镇的并不只有苦迦菩提。如今这座城镇已经回归现代时代，邻近受诅咒城市司泽的幽灵总督周明霞也注意到了这里。她长期觊觎生长于柳岸镇腹地的珍贵木材，尤其是山中的杉树；木材大亨马戈凯在前一年未能将这批货物运送至她的木场，此事很可能会引来她更直接的行动。若真如此，周明霞会在 PCs 于现世度过的第一个夏天中的某个时刻，试图对柳岸镇主张权利。

周明霞的阴谋建立在龙华古法中一项鲜为人知的条文之上：若某位总督是通过非法方式任命，或对其封地弃置不顾达一年零一日，那么为了保护平民并确保治理稳定，另一位合法任命的总督便可对该领地提出主张。随着柳岸镇在消失 115 年后诡异地重返世间，明霞宣称这项条文已被违反了百余次，因此坚持认为自己理应有权统治这座城镇（以及其周边资源），将其纳为己有。

由于周明霞是个妄想的幽灵，她的主张实际上是否成立并不重要。她只需要一个再薄弱不过的借口，就足以把她的亡灵爪牙派进柳岸镇；而一旦她在自己心中认定这项主张合法，便会立刻这么做。PCs 应当刚好有足够时间在明霞派出亡灵大军吞并柳岸镇前收到警告，而他们的首要任务就是击败这支军队。

如果 PCs 击败了这支入侵部队，周明霞会花些时间考虑自己的下一步动作。此时，当地律师骆熙旸想出了一条也许能永久击败这名幽灵的计策。这一次，这位律师对如今早已过时的龙华律法的深刻了解终于派上了用场：她援引了一种可剥夺明霞总督之位的法律机制，并相信这名幽灵内在的逻辑会迫使她接受这一裁决，从而将她永久解除，并使司泽摆脱她可怖的掌控。

要将明霞逐下权位，PCs 必须从司泽周边的每一位总督那里取得一致的不信任投票，然后将他们的签名收集到一卷正式的谴责文书上。当周明霞面对这卷文书时，她将别无选择，只能羞愧退位，因为龙华律法白纸黑字地如此规定。

然而，要取得这些签名绝非易事。除了 PCs 之外，还有三位总督的印玺与签名必须取得。

牡丹白夫人是一名将白芳山视为自己领地的络新妇。她虚荣而喜好奢华，是个普通的络新妇，深深沉溺于她们宫廷中的种种权谋。想要赢得她的印玺，可能需要一笔相当可观的贿赂，或者在宫廷权谋游戏中对抗牡丹夫人的竞争对手。

乌帕罗·卡总督是乌帕罗家族年迈的家主，统治着亚木镇。PCs 造访这座城镇时，会发现乌帕罗家族的祖宅已经被废弃。贵族与仆役全都消失无踪，只留下他们的牙齿。枕头上、厨房台面上以及其他地方散落着牙齿，这景象怪异至极。

通过与亚木的村民交谈，并研究宅邸中留下的线索，PCs 可以查明，这一家人是在大约一年前一个无月之夜失踪的，而村民们因为太惧怕络新妇，不敢将这件事告知他人。若想找到并救出乌帕罗家族，PCs 必须在一次日全食期间，由一位 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.aTYy1WHwAZiuei4h]{月夜尊} 的祭司用神圣经文涂满他们的全身。如此一来，他们便能进入精魂世界，查明乌帕罗家族的遭遇——也就是乌帕罗·卡中了一个伪装成凡人顾问的萨奇尔的圈套，并在无意间允许对方将他的整个家族拖入希巴尔巴，也就是萨奇尔们位于以太位面的国度。如今，乌帕罗全家都被囚禁于苦难折磨之中，而 PCs 必须找到并救出他们，才能争取到他的投票。

一知苏萨璐夫人是夜莺谷的统治者，也是 PCs 最后一位必须恳求的总督。一知夫人是一位优雅却满怀怨愤的女子，如今已年近七十；只有在 PCs 找回并以复活术复生她儿子朧的骸骨后，她才会在文书上签字。朧多年前被络新妇掳走。

要完成这项任务，PCs 必须在阴司察夕地下宫殿下方的尸骸堆中找到他的遗骸。朧是在 30 年前被带走的，而他在络新妇手中活过一年的可能性都很低。若他的俘虏者没有拿走，一条小巧的银夜莺项链也许能帮助辨认出他的骸骨。尽管识别、取回并复原朧的任务几乎不可能完成，一知夫人却毫不动摇：如果 PCs 想要她的帮助，就必须满足这一要求。她认为，像他们这样强大的人物，理应能做到这一点。

一旦 PCs 取得全部三份签名，他们便可以向司泽进军，击败其中的亡灵守护者与死灵护，并直面周明霞总督。面对那卷文书与龙华律法的法条，明霞必须承认自己权威的丧失，而她的幽灵也终于迈向来世。

此后，司泽将重获自由——而且需要一位新的总督。

The Ghostly Governor

Kugaptee wasn’t the only menace threatening Willowshore. Now that the town has returned to the modern era, Chou Mingxia, the ghostly governor of the nearby cursed city of Sze, takes note. She has long coveted the precious lumber that grows in Willowshore’s hinterlands, particularly the sugi trees in its mountains; the lumber lord Mago Kai’s failure to deliver this product to her stockyards the previous year may well result in more direct action. If so, Chou Mingxia attempts to assert a claim against Willowshore at some point during the first summer the PCs spend in the living world.

Chou Mingxia’s scheme is based on a little-known provision in the old laws of Lung Wa, which state that if a governor is illegitimately appointed or neglects their fiefdom for a year and a day, then in the interest of protecting the citizenry and ensuring stable governance, another duly appointed governor can lay claim to that territory. With the strange return of Willowshore to the world after 115 years, Mingxia claims that the provision has been violated more than a hundred times and takes the stance that she should be entitled to govern the town (and its regional resources) as her own.

Because Chou Mingxia is a deluded ghost, the actual merits of her claim aren’t important. She needs only the thinnest of pretexts to send her undead minions into Willowshore, which she does as soon as she’s satisfied in her own mind that her claim is legitimate. The PCs should have just enough time to be warned of Mingxia’s plans before she sends an army of undead to annex Willowshore, and their first task is defeating this army.

If the PCs defeat this invading force, Chou Mingxia takes some time to consider her next actions. At this point, local lawyer Luo Xi Yang hits upon a stratagem that might permanently defeat the ghost. For once, the lawyer’s deep familiarity with the now-outdated laws of Lung Wa pays off: she cites a legal mechanism for stripping Mingxia of her governorship, and she believes that the ghost’s internal logic will force her to bow to this decision, which will permanently dispel her and free Sze from her awful grip.

To remove Mingxia from power, the PCs must secure a unanimous vote of no confidence from every governor around Sze, then gather their signatures into an official scroll of condemnation. When faced with this scroll, Chou Mingxia will have no choice but to abdicate in shame, for it’s written in the laws of Lung Wa.

Securing the signatures, however, won’t be easy. In addition to the PCs, there are three governors whose seals and signatures must be obtained.

Lady Mudan Bai is a jorogumo who claims White Fragrance Mountain as her domain. Vain and fond of luxury, she’s a typical jorogumo and deeply immersed in the schemes of their court. Winning her seal is likely to require either a significant bribe or playing courtly games of intrigue against Lady Mudan’s rivals.

Governor Uparo Ka, the elderly patriarch of House Uparo, rules over the town of Yamu. Upon visiting this town, the PCs find that the ancestral Uparo estate has been abandoned. The nobles and servants have vanished, leaving only their teeth behind. It’s a strange sight to find teeth lying on pillows, fallen on kitchen countertops, and so forth.

By talking to the villagers of Yamu and studying clues left in the house, the PCs can ascertain that the family vanished on a moonless night approximately one year ago, and that the villagers were too afraid of the jorogumo to bring this occurrence to their attention. To find and rescue the Uparo family, the PCs must have their entire bodies painted with holy sutras by a priest of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.aTYy1WHwAZiuei4h]{Tsukiyo} during a full solar eclipse. Doing so will enable them to pass into the spirit world and find out what happened to the Uparo family—namely, that Uparo Ka fell victim to a sahkil posing as a mortal advisor and inadvertently permitted them to drag his entire household into Xibalba, the sahkils’ realm on the Ethereal Plane. Now, the entire Uparo household is imprisoned in torment, and the PCs must find and rescue them to secure his vote.

Lady Ichi Susarru, the ruler of Nightingales’ Hollow, is the final governor to whom the PCs must appeal. Lady Ichi is an elegant but embittered woman, now in her late sixties, who will sign the scroll only if the PCs recover and resurrect the bones of her son, Oboru, who was seized by the jorogumo years before.

To accomplish this task, the PCs must find his remains amid the charnel heaps beneath the subterranean palaces of Yin-Sichasi. Oboru was taken 30 years ago, and it’s unlikely that he survived more than a year with the jorogumo. Only a small, silver nightingale necklace might identify his bones, if his captors didn’t take it. Although the task of identifying, retrieving, and restoring Oboru is nigh impossible, Lady Ichi is immovable: if the PCs want her help, then they must fulfill this demand. Such powerful people, she reasons, should be able to do it.

Once the PCs have secured all three signatures, they can march on Sze, defeat its undead guardians and necromantic wards, and confront Governor Chou Mingxia. Faced with the scroll and the dictates of Lung Wa’s laws, Mingxia must concede the loss of her authority, and her spirit finally moves on to the afterlife.

Thereafter, Sze is free—and will need a new governor.

Shinzo’s Legacy.name: 信藏的遗产 Shinzo’s Legacy
Shinzo’s Legacy.text:
信藏的遗产

神秘的信藏向PC们揭示了他本质的真相——他是一位侍奉@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QZD0u1jxwz0kj8uI]{法拉斯玛}的强大代理者，被称为死神——随后，他最后一次造访了柳岸镇。随着这座城镇重返生者世界，他在拨乱反正一事上的个人牵连也已结束；若PC们不进一步采取行动，他的故事今后将不再与他们的人生交汇。

然而，PC们或许已经与这位神秘商人结下了友谊；如今他们既已守住柳岸镇，也已强大到足以开始穿行诸位面，他们便可能去寻找这位老朋友，看看自己是否能回报他在肆季鬼志期间给予他们的恩情。

信藏之所以对柳岸镇如此在意，部分原因要追溯到数十年前——早在这座城镇陷入其心景之前——他曾犯下过一次触怒法拉斯玛的过失。由于引魂使翼被指派在他身边，某种意义上充当监视者，信藏被禁止直接干预凡人生死的命运；但那些被困在柳岸镇中的人，既非活人，也非死者。困于两者之间，信藏希望自己能通过提供力所能及的协助（而且只能间接相助，以免进一步激怒法拉斯玛），重新赢得这位女神的信任。

如果PC们前往骨园寻找他，那么无论法拉斯玛是否已经接受了他的工作，以此作为对那次过失的偿付，都由你决定；至于那次过失本身的性质，也同样由你裁定。也许信藏曾擅自处决那些被他判定为不配活下去的凡人，并因此偏离了自己作为公正死亡裁断者的职责。也可能是他的贪欲驱使他接受那些本应死去之人的报酬，让他们得以苟延残喘，多活上几年。又或者，他爱上了一名凡人，并采取手段确保爱侣得以长久存活，而不是冒着对方死后转变成某种全新存在的风险。

如果你决定信藏尚未偿清债务，那么当PC们去寻找他时，他们应当得知法拉斯玛已将他派去执行一项尤其危险的任务，以完成赎罪。这个危险任务应与他的过失性质相符。若信藏曾是个以己意裁决他人生死的处刑者，那么他可能会被指派去监督一个注定毁灭的偏远世界迎来终结，而那里的居民正竭力挣扎，试图避免末日降临。若信藏贪婪成性，他可能会被派去守望骨园某处一座藏匿的宝库，而那里如今已遭邪恶精魂围攻。若信藏曾爱上凡人又失去了对方，他可能会被派往一个世界，在那里，他昔日的爱侣已经转生，而他必须遵从命令，只能旁观其人生而不得施加影响，如此他才能终于见证自己所爱的那段故事本应如何落幕。当PC们最终追上信藏时，他们应发现这位死神正陷于冲突之中，并且即将失败。PC们决定是鼓舞他、保护他，还是为他出谋划策，将决定他是否还能再次毫无限制地侍奉法拉斯玛，抑或将作为最终惩罚被转化为原初的第五元素。

Shinzo’s Legacy

The mysterious Shinzo reveals to the PCs the truth of his nature—that he’s a powerful agent of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QZD0u1jxwz0kj8uI]{Pharasma} known as a shinigami—before he pays his final visit to Willowshore. With the town’s return to the living world, his personal stake in setting things right has concluded, and without further action on the PCs’ behalf, his story will no longer intersect with their own.

Yet the PCs might have formed a bond of friendship with the mysterious merchant, and now that they’ve secured Willowshore and become powerful enough to begin traveling the planes, they might seek out their old friend to see if they can return the favor he extended to them during Season of Ghosts.

Part of Shinzo’s interest in Willowshore ties back to an old infraction against Pharasma he made decades before the town became mired in its mindscape. With the psychopomp Yix assigned to him as a minder of sorts, Shinzo was barred from directly intervening in the fate of mortal lives, but those trapped in Willowshore were neither living nor dead. Trapped in between, Shinzo hoped that by providing what aid he could (and only indirectly assisting so he would not further aggravate Pharasma), he could earn back the goddess’s trust.

If the PCs seek him out in the Boneyard, whether or not Pharasma has accepted his work as payment for his infraction is left to you to decide, as is the nature of the infraction in the first place. Perhaps Shinzo took it upon himself to execute mortals he judged as being unworthy of life, and in so doing stepped out of his role as an impartial arbiter of death. Maybe his greed pushed him to accept payments from those who should’ve died so they could eke out a few more years of life. Or perhaps he fell in love with a mortal and took steps to ensure his lover’s lasting life rather than risk their transformation after death into something new.

If you decide that Shinzo hasn’t yet paid his debt, then when the PCs seek him out, they should learn Pharasma has sent him on a particularly dangerous mission to complete his penance. This dangerous task should match the nature of his infraction. If Shinzo was a judgmental executioner, he might be assigned the task of overseeing the end of a remote world destined for destruction while its inhabitants scramble to prevent their doom. An avaricious Shinzo could be assigned to stand vigil over a hidden vault somewhere in the Boneyard that has become besieged by evil spirits. If Shinzo loved and lost a mortal, he might be sent to a world where his one-time lover has reincarnated and must comply with orders to observe their life without influencing it, so he can finally witness how his love’s story was supposed to end. When the PCs finally catch up with Shinzo, they should find the shinigami at odds and about to fail. Their decision to bolster, protect, or advise him should mean the difference in whether he’s ever allowed to serve Pharasma without restriction again or if he shall be transformed into raw quintessence as a final punishment.

Continuing the Campaign.name: 延续战役 Continuing the Campaign
Continuing the Campaign.text:
延续战役

随着柳岸镇重返生者的世界、赫山宝的灵魂获得解放、苦迦菩提再度在自己的坟墓中归于沉寂，PC们的家乡已经安全了，但他们的冒险未必就此结束。

本节概述了一些将队伍的冒险扩展到天夏各地的选项。这些建议应被视为延续战役的起点，让你能根据PC们的兴趣与优先事项展开合适的战役，而不是一张刻在石头上的铁路线图。

由于PC们在继续前进之前，应当有充足的机会在柳岸镇休息、放松，并庆祝他们的胜利，这份纲要将何时继续、以及是否继续这段征途的决定权交给他们自己。如果他们对自己已经取得的结果感到满足，故事到这里结束也未尝不可。

然而，如果他们决定继续前进……

Continuing the Campaign

With Willowshore returned to the living world, Heh Shan-Bao’s soul set free, and Kugaptee once more quiet in his grave, the PCs’ hometown is safe, but their adventures don’t have to come to an end.

This section outlines some options for extending the party’s adventures in Tian Xia. These suggestions should be taken as a starting point to continue with a campaign that suits your PCs’ interests and priorities, not as a railroad map etched in stone.

Because the PCs should have ample opportunity to rest, relax, and celebrate their victories in Willowshore before moving on, this outline leaves it up to them to decide when and if they want to continue their quest. If they’re content with the result they’ve achieved, the story can end there.

However, should they decide to press on...

First Long Night.name: 第一长夜 First Long Night

Black Sesame Soup with Peanut-filled Glu.name: 花生馅糯米黑芝麻汤 Black Sesame Soup with Peanut-filled Glutinous Ric
Black Sesame Soup with Peanut-filled Glu.text:
黑芝麻糊配花生馅汤圆

这些营养丰富、带着坚果香气的汤品，颜色如同神门昏暗天空一般漆黑，带有烘烤后的微苦回甘，常被当作晚间甜点食用，以强健身体，抵御夜晚寒冷潮湿的天气。糯米汤圆有时也会加入其中，内里常包着花生碎；这些汤圆带来额外的甜蜜惊喜，也提醒食客，即使在最黑暗的夜晚，也依然可能有不为人知的喜悦。

原料

2杯烘烤黑芝麻

1/2杯茉莉香米

3 1/2块岩石糖

1/2汤匙盐

2汤匙烘烤芝麻油

12杯水

1碗糯米粉

1碗烘香花生碎

1/4杯糖

  • 将烘烤过的黑芝麻磨成细粉。
  • 把芝麻粉、茉莉香米、岩石糖、盐和烘烤芝麻油放入锅中。
  • 往锅中加入6杯水。
  • 煮至微沸后转小火慢煮，因为缓慢烹饪能让芝麻汤更加顺滑。
  • 接下来一到两小时内，定时搅拌，使汤的质地更均匀；让米粒彻底煮熟并融入汤中。视需要加水，并注意别让汤烧焦。
  • 将糯米粉加少量水混合，揉捏成团。若面团变得太稀，就再加些水以保持弹性；同时注意别让外皮破裂。
  • 把面团揪成面皮，每张约宽1 1/2英寸（3.8厘米）。
  • 将糖与烘香花生碎混合，做成馅料。
  • 每张面皮包入馅料，再捏合封口，搓成圆球。
  • 另取一口锅，放入汤圆和6杯水，煮至沸腾。小心搅拌，确保汤圆不会粘在锅边或汤勺上。待汤圆浮上水面后，将其捞出，放入芝麻汤中。
  • 将芝麻汤和汤圆分别盛入小碗中。温热时食用。

Black Sesame Soup with Peanut-filled Glutinous Rice Balls

These nutritious, nutty soups, as black as Shenmen’s ill-lit skies, possess a roasted, bittersweet tinge and are often consumed as evening desserts to fortify the body against the night’s cold and damp weather. Glutinous rice balls, often filled with ground peanuts, are sometimes added; these rice balls provide an additional sweet surprise and remind diners of the possibility of hidden joys even on the darkest nights.

Ingredients

2 cups roasted black sesame seeds

1/2 cup jasmine rice

3 1/2 chunks rock sugar

1/2 tablespoon salt

2 tablespoons roasted sesame oil

12 cups water

1 bowl glutinous rice flour

1 bowl toasted ground peanuts

1/4 cup sugar

  • Ground the roasted sesame seeds into fine powder.
  • Place the roasted sesame powder, jasmine rice, rock sugar, salt, and roast sesame oil into a pot.
  • Add 6 cups of water into the pot.
  • Bring to a simmer and cook on low heat, as you want slow cooking for a smoother soup.
  • Over the next hour or two, stir regularly to even out the texture of the soup; let the rice grains be totally cooked and absorbed into the soup. Add water as needed, and be careful not to let the soup burn.
  • Mix the glutinous rice flour with a bit of water, and pinch into dough. If the dough becomes too thin, add more water to retain its elasticity; be careful not to let the skin break.
  • Pinch the dough into wrappers, each approximately 1 1/2 inches (3.8 cm) wide.
  • Mix the sugar and toasted ground peanuts to get the filling.
  • Stuff each wrapper with filling, and pinch to seal into balls.
  • In a separate pot, add the rice balls and 6 cups of water, and bring to a boil. Stir carefully to ensure the rice balls don’t stick to the sides of the pot or the ladle. Once the rice balls float to the top, remove them and deposit into the sesame soup.
  • Serve the soup and rice balls in small bowls. Eat when warm.

Shenmen Salt and Pepper Mooncakes.name: 神门椒盐月饼 Shenmen Salt and Pepper Mooncakes
Shenmen Salt and Pepper Mooncakes.text:
神门椒盐月饼

这些轻薄酥脆的烘焙点心在神门很受欢迎，人们常用它们来纪念第一长夜的丰收月。尽管更讲究身份的食客可能会鄙夷这些辛香、近似饼干的圆饼，认为它们算不上“正经月饼”，但在物资匮乏的神门，各地村庄都推崇这种层次分明的酥点所带来的咸香、椒辣与柑橘气息交织的风味。

原料

1汤匙白胡椒粉（可按口味增减）

1汤匙玫瑰浸糖

1 1/2茶匙盐（可按口味增减）

2把压碎的橘皮

2杯炸红葱头

1杯芝麻

1杯瓜子

1份天书酥皮面团（也称天书水油面团），擀成24×24英寸的薄片（约60×60厘米）

1杯猪油

2个蛋黄，打散

  • 将烤箱预热至350°F（180°C）。
  • 制作馅料：将各1杯红葱头、橘皮和两种种子混合后铺在烤盘上，烘烤至种子变黄。然后倒入碗中放凉。
  • 将胡椒、糖、盐和剩余的红葱头均匀拌入并揉进酥皮面团中。若面团太干，可加入猪油。
  • 将揉好的面团分成8个3×3英寸（约7.5×7.5厘米）的面团球。
  • 将每个面团球再次混合揉捏。按需加入猪油，使质地更顺滑。
  • 将红葱头、橘皮和种子的馅料等分，并给每个面团球分配1份等量馅料。
  • 将每个面团球捏合封口，压平成圆饼，再次捏合使其封口均匀。确保面皮尽可能薄，但不要让馅料露出。
  • 将封好的酥点排放在铺好烘焙纸的烤盘上，并在每个表面刷上蛋液。
  • 放入烤箱中层烘烤约20分钟，或烤至金黄褐色。
  • 月饼配茶一同食用，最好是发酵茶或陈茶。

Shenmen Salt and Pepper Mooncakes

These thin, flaky baked goods are popular in Shenmen for commemorating the harvest moon of First Long Night. While more patrician diners might scorn these peppery biscuit-like discs as not being “proper mooncakes,” villages across resource-scarce Shenmen swear by these layered pastries’ swirl of savory saltiness, peppery heat, and citrus notes.

Ingredients

1 tablespoon white pepper powder (add or reduce to taste)

1 tablespoon rose-infused sugar

1 1/2 teaspoons salt (add or reduce to taste)

2 handfuls crushed tangerine peels

2 cups fried shallots

1 cup sesame seeds

1 cup melon seeds

1 portion Tian-Shu flaky pastry dough (also known as Tian-Shu water-oil dough), rolled out into a 24×24 inch sheet (approximately 60×60 cm)

1 cup lard

2 egg yolks, beaten

  • Heat oven to 350°F (180°C).
  • Make the filling by mixing 1 cup each of shallots, peels, and both seeds onto a baking tray, and bake until the seeds turn yellow. Then pour them out into a bowl to cool.
  • Mix and knead the pepper, sugar, salt, and remaining shallots evenly into the pastry dough. If the dough is too dry, add lard.
  • Separate the kneaded dough into 8 3×3 inch (approximately 7.5×7.5 cm) balls.
  • Mix and knead each ball again. Add lard as needed to smoothen the texture.
  • Separate the filling of shallots, peels, and seeds into equal portions, and allocate 1 equal portion to each ball of dough.
  • Pinch each ball to seal them, flatten them into discs, and pinch again to seal them evenly. Ensure the dough is as thin as possible without letting the filling stick out.
  • Arrange the sealed pastries on a lined baking sheet, and brush each with beaten egg.
  • Bake for about 20 minutes in the middle of the oven, or until golden brown.
  • Serve mooncakes with tea, preferably fermented or aged.

Festival Foods.name: 节日食物 Festival Foods
Festival Foods.text:
节日食物

以下两种点心在第一长夜期间极受欢迎。

Festival Foods

The following two treats are wildly popular during First Long Night.

Festival Fashion.name: 节日风尚 Festival Fashion
Festival Fashion.text:
节日风尚

尽管第一长夜期间所穿的具体样式与服饰会因城镇而异，但在神门各地，某些标志性的元素始终延续至今。

轻装武备

带有能赋予持久照明效果魔法的武器很受欢迎，因为它们既可充当光源，又能在需要时用于防身。虽然并非所有不死生物都具有如此强烈的光弱点，但它们全都能在黑暗中视物，而不必腾出一只手来握持火把或提灯，往往就意味着生死之间的差别。

月饼与茶

人们聚在一起分享这些美味点心，它们被做成丰收满月般的形状，并配上浓郁陈年的茶一同享用。更富裕的厨房会在月饼中填入奢华的原料，比如桂花莲蓉和咸蛋；而较为朴素的储藏间则用盐、胡椒、炸红葱头或陈皮碎做出简单的吃食。参加节日的人通常会在腰带上挂一个小藤篮，用来装额外的月饼。

红绳

将红绳系在手腕上，是在向一项 @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog18sangpo]{桑博齐} 根源致意；这种根源认为，这样的丝线能够吸收幽灵的影响，并会在抵御敌对精魂后自行脱落。如果有红绳掉了，除非你想让不死生物再次登门，否则千万别捡起来！相反，就让它们在冬季的风暴中被冲走吧。

微型提灯

并不是所有人都买得起发光武器，而即便买得起的人，也常会佩戴一盏微型提灯，按传统用短链挂在腰带或带扣上。在夜晚将尽、太阳升起前的最后几分钟点亮这盏私人的提灯，象征着第一长夜的结束。

与蟋蟀共饮

村民们经常把蟋蟀喂给蜘蛛，希望借此压住那些爱告密的家伙（以吵闹的蟋蟀为象征），并象征性地满足络新妇的食欲。到了秋天，许多人会为这些蟋蟀的精魂留下小小一碗含酒精的谷物糊，既是请求宽恕，也是感谢它们作为牺牲替代品所扮演的角色。参加节日的人常会随身带几只小葫芦容器盛放酒精，以便在需要时给空碗续上；或者也会带着装有蟋蟀的小藤笼，好把它们喂给蜘蛛。

披戴森林

为了抵御雨雪，参加节日的人偏爱披风、斗笠，以及用涂蜡稻草或竹子制成的鞋子。这些材料随处可见，天然防水，也便于加工。它们带着泥土感的褐色，在神门那片充满怪物的荒野中还能提供出色而又负担得起的伪装。当地人把这种做法称为“披戴森林”。

Festival Fashion

While exact styles and outfits worn during First Long Night can vary from town to town, certain touchstones persist throughout Shenmen.

Lightly Armed

Weapons bearing magic that impart lasting illumination are popular for serving as light sources that can be used for defense as needed. While not all undead possess such extreme light vulnerability, they can all see in the dark, and not having to have a hand free to hold a torch or lantern can mean the difference between life and death.

Mooncakes and Tea

Communities gather to share these delicacies, shaped like the fullness of the harvest moon, pairing them alongside strong, aged tea. Wealthier kitchens stuff mooncakes with luxurious ingredients, such as osmanthus-infused lotus paste and salted eggs, while humbler pantries conjure simpler fare from salt, pepper, fried shallots, or crushed tangerine peel. A festival-goer typically travels with a small wicker basket on the belt to hold extra mooncakes.

Red Strings

By wearing red strings around the wrist, festival-goers honor a @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog18sangpo]{Sangpotshi} tradition that asserts such threads absorb ghostly influence and fall off after resisting hostile spirits. If one falls, don’t pick them up unless you wish for return visits from the undead! Instead, leave them to be washed away by winter’s storms.

Miniature Lanterns

Not everyone can afford a glowing weapon, and even those who do often wear a single miniature lantern candle that’s traditionally hooked via a short chain to a belt or buckle. Lighting this personal lantern in the last minutes of the night as the sun rises symbolizes the end of First Long Night.

Drinking with the Crickets

Villagers regularly feed crickets to spiders, hoping to discourage tattletales (represented by the noisy crickets) and symbolically satiate the jorogumo’s hungers. In fall, many leave tiny bowls of alcoholic grain-mush as overtures to these crickets’ spirits, both to beg forgiveness as well as give thanks for their roles as sacrificial proxies. Festival-goers often carry a few small gourd containers to carry alcohol so they can refill empty bowls as needed or, alternatively, small wicker cages that contain crickets that can be fed to spiders.

Wearing the Forest

To ward off rain and snow, festival-goers favor capes, conical hats, and shoes of waxed straw or bamboo. These materials are ever-present, naturally water-repellent, and easy to work with. Their muddy browns also provide admirable yet affordable camouflage within Shenmen’s monster-filled wilderness. Locals refer to this practice as “wearing the forest.”

Lantern Making.name: 制作天灯 Lantern Making
Lantern Making.text:
制作天灯

天灯最初是在舒国的时代为传递军事信号而发明的。如今，这项古老习俗已有了不同的文化意义：象征重逢，以及人们的愿望找到通往天际的道路。

这些天灯以竹篾为骨架，用涂油的稻纸制成。其装饰常采用鸟类（但绝不会是乌鸦或渡鸦，因为声名远播的络新妇极其厌恶天狗）、龙，以及其他飞行生物等奇巧造型。

有一段时间，蜘蛛曾是提灯设计中极受欢迎的主题，或许是为了向络新妇统治者献媚；不过，这一风潮在数年前便失宠了。一些想讨好琅蕾夫人的官员曾资助举办了一场盛大的制灯庆典，并委托制作了一盏巨大的金色圆网蛛造型提灯，其规模之大，甚至遮蔽了丰收月。然而，这盏巨型提灯最终以极为惊人的方式坠毁。随后引发的大火烧毁了数栋建筑，但其中一尊琅蕾夫人的大型雕像也在波及中被毁，因此她公开指控并惩罚了涉事官员与工匠，罪名是鼓励不敬与煽动叛乱。

经历了这场如此不祥的事故后，大多数制灯庆典又恢复了乡间、较不张扬的形式。作为对其军事功用起源的恰当呼应，如今各村庄也会利用制灯庆典进行基本通讯。尽管络新妇对学识的清洗导致了诸如信号技术等专门知识的流失，人们仍然能够借由放飞天灯来传递简单却至关重要的信息。在第一长夜，如果地平线上布满飞舞的灯火，许多人便会因此安心，知道邻村的人们仍然活着，并且还能制作天灯。相反，如果附近某个村庄在这一重要节日没有放出自己的天灯，那就很可能意味着他们已遭幽灵或更糟之物所害。在这种情况下，邻近村庄可能会派出最勇敢的成员前去调查、提供协助，并在必要时为不得安息的死者施行驱邪。

一场制灯庆典包括两小时的提灯设计与制作，最后将所有提灯同时点亮并放飞；比赛的获胜者，是那盏最能激起观众赞叹的提灯。在此期间，玩家角色需要进行四次制作检定以决定结果。

制灯庆典

  • 专注
  • 探索

技能检定 @Check[crafting|dc:19]

Lantern Making

Sky Lanterns were originally developed during the days of Shu for sending military signals. The ancient practice now has a different cultural significance: representing reunions and people’s wishes finding their way to the heavens.

These sky lanterns have bamboo frames and are made of oiled rice paper. They incorporate decor of fanciful shapes like birds (but never crows or ravens, due to the famed jorogumo’s intense dislike of tengu), dragons, and other flying creatures.

For a while, spiders were extremely popular motifs for lantern design, perhaps as a sign of flattery to the jorogumo overlords; however, that trend fell out of favor several years ago. Officials wishing to curry Lady Lang Loi’s favor sponsored a grand lantern making ceremony and commissioned a massive lantern shaped like a golden orb-weaver spider, which was so large it eclipsed even the harvest moon. This gigantic lantern eventually crashed in spectacular fashion. The ensuing conflagration burned down several buildings, but the collateral destruction of a large statue of Lady Lang Loi resulted in her public accusations and punishments against the officials and artisans involved, on charges of encouraging disrespect and fomenting rebellion.

After such an inauspicious incident, most lantern making ceremonies have resumed their rural, less high-profile focus. In a fitting nod to its functional military origins, villages now also use lantern making ceremonies for basic communications. While the jorogumo purge on scholarship has led to a loss of specialized knowledge like signaling techniques, it’s still possible to share simple yet vital information with released sky lanterns. On First Long Night, if the horizons are filled with flying lights, it reassures many to know their neighbors are still alive and able to construct sky lanterns. On the contrary, if a nearby village doesn’t release its own sky lanterns on this important festival, it’s very possible they’ve fallen to ghosts or worse. In such situations, neighboring villages might dispatch their bravest members to investigate, bring aid, and, if necessary, provide exorcisms for the unquiet dead.

A lantern making ceremony involves two hours of designing and crafting lanterns, culminating in the lighting and release of them all at once; the winner of the contest is the one whose lantern evokes the most admiration from the spectators. The PC attempts four Crafting checks during this time to determine results.

Lantern Making Ceremony

  • Concentrate
  • Exploration

Bundle-Cutting.name: 割草绳 Bundle-Cutting
Bundle-Cutting.text:
割草绳

在围观同伴的鼓舞下，割草绳比赛的参与者奋力将悬挂着的一捆捆稻草从编织紧密的格架上割落。这项比赛还有一个额外的变化：每位参与者在比赛开始时，手脚都会被细绳松松绑住。石制匕首被放在稍远处的地面上，因此参与者必须先解开自己身上的束缚，然后冲去取回匕首，最后再跑回来，在时限内尽可能多地割下草捆。

割草绳起源于训练村民应对被土匪擒获捆绑，或落入林地陷阱时的演练——这些技巧同样有助于逃离巨蜘蛛及其他长期威胁本地居民的生物所结的蛛网，甚至早在络新妇统治之前便已如此。参与者一旦挣脱自身束缚，再去割断其他束缚，就象征着迅速行动，救援并释放被捆住的盟友。

当然，这类训练同样可用于对付络新妇的蛛丝缠缚。为了减少怀疑并淡化煽动叛乱的意味，这里使用的绳索和绳结都被设计得尽可能不像蛛网。比赛中高声唱起的农业歌谣，也同样让城中那些附庸者与占据此地的络新妇那挑剔的耳朵感到不适。因此，在这场伴随着笑声、歌声与喝彩、看似无害的比赛中，神门的人民在众目睽睽之下磨练着自己的技能。也许有朝一日，这些技能所切开的将不只是稻草，还会是丝质蛛网与斑驳甲壳。

与其他比赛相比，这项比赛的节奏快得多；普通的一场割草绳通常会在1到2分钟内结束，具体取决于所选的歌曲（无论时间长短，比赛仍通过四次技能检定来决定结果）。

割草绳比赛

  • 专注
  • 探索

技能检定 @Check[thievery|dc:17], @Check[athletics|dc:19], @Check[survival|dc:21]

特殊 在尝试任何技能检定之前，参与者必须先从自身束缚中挣脱（DC 17）。如果参与者在第一次尝试时便成功挣脱，他们就能在没有减值的情况下进行四次技能检定，以赢得割草绳比赛。如果参与者需要两次挣脱尝试才能脱困，则其四次技能检定承受–1环境减值。如果参与者需要三次或四次挣脱尝试才能脱困，则其后续技能检定承受–2环境减值。第五次挣脱尝试必定成功，但此后该参与者的后续技能检定承受–3环境减值。

Bundle-Cutting

Encouraged by onlooking fellows, participants in bundle-cutting contests strive to cut hanging bundles of straw loose from tightly-woven lattices. There’s an additional twist to this contest, as each participant begins the contest loosely bound hand and foot in twine ropes. Stone daggers are laid on the ground some distance away so that participants must first undo their own bindings, then dash to retrieve daggers, and finally run back to cut as many bundles free as they can within a time limit.

Bundle-cutting evolved from training exercises to help villagers deal with being captured and bound by bandits or caught in woodland traps—techniques that are equally useful in escaping the webs of the giant spiders and similar creatures who have long posed dangers to the locals, even before jorogumo rule. Once a participant escapes their bindings, the cutting of other bindings represent swift action to rescue and release allies who have been bound.

Such exercises, of course, have applications in overcoming the webbing of jorogumo as well. To reduce suspicions and shed implications of sedition, the ropes and knots are designed to look as unlike webs as possible. The loud farming songs sung during these games are also off-putting to the sophisticated eardrums of city-dwelling collaborators and jorogumo occupiers alike. Thus, through this innocuous contest punctuated by laughter, song, and cheering, Shenmen’s people sharpen their skills in plain sight. Perhaps these skills might be used one day not simply to slice straw, but also to cut through silken webs and mottled carapaces.

This contest is much faster-paced than the others, with a typical bout of bundle-cutting resolving over the course of 1 to 2 minutes, depending on the song chosen (regardless of the time, the contest still resolves via four skill checks).

Bundle-Cutting Contest

  • Concentrate
  • Exploration

Skill Checks @Check[thievery|dc:17], @Check[athletics|dc:19], @Check[survival|dc:21]

Special Before any skill checks can be attempted, a participant must Escape (DC 17) from their bonds. If a participant Escapes on their first attempt, they can attempt the four skill checks to win bundle-cutting without penalty. If a participant requires two Escape attempts to get free, they take a –1 circumstance penalty to their four skill checks. If a participant requires three or four Escape attempts to get free, their following skill checks take a –2 circumstance penalty. A fifth Escape attempt is always successful, but after this, the participant takes a –3 circumstance penalty to their following skill checks.

Admiring the Moon.name: 赏月 Admiring the Moon
Admiring the Moon.text:
咏月诗会

咏月诗会是一种根植于自仪兴宫廷侍臣文化的游戏。参与者面向丰收之月聚集一处，一边享用月饼与茶，一边吟诗作文，赞颂明月的优雅与美丽。辞藻典雅、意境动人的诗句会赢得喝彩与称赞，而较为雕琢的比喻与警句则会引来鼓励与点评。随着夜晚渐深，茶总会被酒与烈酒取代，诗作也会逐渐让位于对形而上学与政治哲学的讨论。

一场普通的咏月诗会通常会持续一小时，其间包括饮食、饮酒、社交与作诗。

咏月诗会

  • 专注
  • 探索

技能检定 @Check[art-lore|dc:17], @Check[performance|dc:19], @Check[religion|dc:21]

Admiring the Moon

Admiring the Moon is a game with roots in Yixing courtier culture. Facing the harvest moon, participants gather to enjoy mooncakes and tea while composing poetry to extol the moon’s grace and beauty. Elegant wordplay and evocative verse win accolades and praises, while more labored metaphors and epigrams spur encouragements and critiques. As the night goes on, tea is invariably replaced with wine and spirits, and poetry gives way to discussions on metaphysics and political philosophy.

A typical bout of Admiring the Moon involves an hour of eating, drinking, socializing, and composing of poems.

Admiring the Moon

Traditional Contests.name: 传统比赛 Traditional Contests
Traditional Contests.text:
传统比赛

以下三项比赛是第一长夜庆典中传统的重头戏。每项游戏都通过在规定时间内进行四次技能检定来结算，以累积胜利点（Pathfinder GM Core 184）。奖品可能只是荣誉与吹嘘的资本，也可能是实际的贵重物品或声望提升（赢得这些游戏可获得的奖品示例见 @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog07turnin.JournalEntryPage.07week3firstlo00]{Week 3}）。在这场冒险中，默认由单个玩家角色参加一项比赛，且不会与其他玩家角色竞争，而是与同村村民较量。如果玩家角色选择参加这些比赛之一，便可尝试进行四次技能检定来获得胜利点——获得至少4点胜利点的玩家角色赢得比赛，而获得至少6点胜利点的玩家角色则会取得压倒性胜利，并可能获得额外奖励（示例见本冒险的 @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog07turnin.JournalEntryPage.07week3firstlo00]{Week 3}）。

这些比赛中用于获得胜利点的技能检定，其DC默认假定参与者为4级；一方面是因为第一长夜发生在第5章期间，另一方面这个等级也适合作为普通小型城镇与村庄中最有本领的本地人会遇到挑战的标准，并让当地专家有最佳机会获胜。如果你想让不同等级的玩家角色也能受到合适挑战，可以随意提高或降低这些DC。

Traditional Contests

The following three contests serve as traditional highlights for First Long Night festivities. Each of these games are resolved via four skill checks attempted over the course of a set amount of time to accumulate Victory Points (Pathfinder GM Core 184). Prizes can vary from little more than accolades and bragging rights to actual valuables or increases to reputation (examples of prizes that can be earned by winning these games are presented on @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog07turnin.JournalEntryPage.07week3firstlo00]{Week 3}). In this adventure, the assumption is that a single PC takes part in a contest and doesn’t compete against other PCs, instead competing against fellow villagers. A PC can attempt four skill checks to earn Victory Points if they choose to take part in one of these contests—a PC who earns at least 4 Victory Points wins the contest, while a PC who earns at least 6 Victory Points achieves an overwhelming win and might earn additional rewards (see @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog07turnin.JournalEntryPage.07week3firstlo00]{Week 3} of this adventure for examples).

The DCs of the skill checks to earn Victory Points for these contests assume that participants are 4th level, both because it’s during Chapter 5 that First Long Night takes place, and because this level is an appropriate one for the most skilled locals in typical small towns and villages to find challenges and to allow local experts the best chance to win. Feel free to increase or decrease these DCs if you wish to challenge PCs of different levels.

Agility under Oppression.name: 压迫下的应变 Agility under Oppression
Agility under Oppression.text:
压迫下的应变

将五彩缤纷的提灯放上天空、割断绳索、吟诵赞颂明月的诗篇——这些根源或许看起来只是些无关紧要的琐事。然而，它们同时发挥着双重作用：其一，让彼此隔绝的村庄围绕对神门身份的共同想象建立联系；其二，在络新妇那傲慢自大的眼皮底下，暗中磨炼并保留实用的知识与技能。

Agility under Oppression

Releasing colorful lanterns into the sky, cutting ropes, poetry praising the moon—these traditions might appear irrelevant oddments. However, they fulfill twofold purposes: one, they allow isolated villages to bond over shared imaginations of a Shenmen identity; two, they facilitate surreptitious honing and preservation of practical knowledge and skills, right under the jorogumo’s haughty noses.

Seasonal Markets.name: 应季市集 Seasonal Markets
Seasonal Markets.text:
应季市集

村庄庆典的喧闹常常会吸引来商人、祭司以及其他访客；当地人很快就会招待这些旅人，并提出用食物、饮料和辛苦积攒的银粉来购买他们的货物和服务。

Seasonal Markets

The hubbub of a village’s celebrations often draws merchants, priests, and other visitors; locals are quick to host such travelers and offer to purchase their goods and services with food, drink, and hard-hoarded silver dust.

Bribing Fumeiyoshi.name: 贿赂文业王 Bribing Fumeiyoshi
Bribing Fumeiyoshi.text:
贿赂文业王

许多人会在墓地附近撒下银粉来贿赂@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.6O4UGWcYERDEugzk]{文业王}，希望他会收下这些供品，不再觉得有必要制造更多亡灵。贪婪的强盗可能会埋伏起来，抢劫村民或私吞那些撒下的银粉；村民对此往往并不介意（只要他们能毫发无伤地脱身），因为这样一来，文业王的怒火反而会降临到那些盗贼身上。

Bribing Fumeiyoshi

Many scatter silver dust near grave sites to bribe @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.6O4UGWcYERDEugzk]{Fumeiyoshi}, hoping he would accept these offerings and not feel the need to create more undead. Greedy bandits might lurk in wait to rob villagers or pocket the strewn silver dust; villagers often don’t mind (providing they escape unharmed), as that simply draws Fumeiyoshi’s wrath upon the thieves instead.

Ghosts... or Ancestors-.name: 幽灵......或祖先？
Ghosts... or Ancestors-.text:
幽灵......或祖先？

神门的一些人对自己变成不死生物的恐惧，还不如亲眼看着挚爱之人经历这般可悲的转变来得强烈。无论如何，他们通过清扫祖坟，防止沉睡的死者苏醒为暴虐的不死生物。有些人会试图驱除那些生前曾是家人的不死生物，并因此将他们净化后的精魂迎回宗族，成为受人尊敬的祖先。

Ghosts... or Ancestors?

Some in Shenmen fear becoming undead less than witnessing loved ones undergoing such pitiable transformations. Regardless, by cleaning ancestral graves, they prevent the sleeping dead from arising as violent undead. Some seek to exorcise undead who were once family, and thus return their purified spirits to the fold as respected ancestors.

Enlightened Self-Interest.name: 良性自利 Enlightened Self-Interest
Enlightened Self-Interest.text:
良性自利

第一长夜期间，许多人会踏上危险的旅程，去行善、清理旧墓，并举行临终仪式。以这种方式帮助其他人——无论生者还是死者——其实也是在帮助自己；毕竟，喂饱邻居或安葬他们，总比去应付由他们饥饿的尸体化成的亡灵要简单得多。

Enlightened Self-Interest

First Long Night sees many embarking on dangerous journeys to do good deeds, clean old graves, and perform last rites. Helping others—be they living or dead—in this way also helps oneself; after all, it’s simpler to feed or bury neighbors rather than deal with undead arising from their starved corpses.

Communal Revivals.name: 人际复兴 Communal Revivals
Communal Revivals.text:
人际复兴

尽管残暴政权的历史已使许多社会纽带破裂，但第一长夜是各个社区重建这些联系的时期。从探望邻近村庄，到为隔壁人家送去食物，每一个微小的举动都让神门的社区再次变得更加紧密。

Communal Revivals

While a history of brutal regimes have fractured many social bonds, First Long Night is a time when communities reforge these connections. From checking on neighboring villages to feeding the families next door, each small step brings Shenmen’s community closer again.

Cold Nights, Warm Hearts.name: 冷夜暖心 Cold Nights, Warm Hearts
Cold Nights, Warm Hearts.text:
冷夜暖心

热甜点（如芝麻花生汤）和泡好的茶会由所有人一同分享，此外还有月饼、汤圆和水果。当地融合的信仰鼓励这种慷慨，认为这样的温暖与团结必定会给来访的祖先或善意的精魂留下深刻印象，而他们之后可能会在未来的年岁里再次归来，并带来好运。

Cold Nights, Warm Hearts

Hot desserts (such as sesame and peanut soup) and brewed tea are shared between all, along with mooncakes, glutinous rice balls, and fruits. Local syncretic beliefs encourage such generosity, stating such warmth and unity are sure to impress visiting ancestors or benevolent spirits who might then return in future years and bring good fortune with them.

Festival Celebrations.name: 节日庆祝 Festival Celebrations
Festival Celebrations.text:
节日庆祝

虽然其他天夏人可能会将第一长夜描述为一场严酷而肃穆的守夜，以对抗冬季与怪物，但神门的居民却将其作为一个怀抱谨慎希望的节日来庆祝；在这一天，他们守护生命中那些微小的欢乐，以免它们被冷酷无情的统治者榨取得一干二净——无论那些统治者是蛛形的、幽灵般的，还是其他类型。以下庆祝活动是第一长夜几种主要的庆祝方式。

Festival Celebrations

While other Tian might characterize First Long Night as a grim, humorless vigil against winter and monsters, Shenmen’s inhabitants celebrate it as a festival of cautious hope, where they protect life’s little joys that might otherwise be drained dry by uncaring overlords, be they arachnid, ghostly, or otherwise. The following celebrations are key among the ways in First Long Night is observed.

First Long Night.name: 第一长夜 First Long Night
First Long Night.text:
第一长夜

随着秋日渐渐让位于愈发漫长的夜晚，居住在神门乡间的人们开始为冬季做准备。这些准备围绕着乡村家庭对第一长夜的庆祝而展开；这是一个家人共度的夜晚，人们以庄重的方式纪念逝去的亲族，同时也见证整个社区怀抱希望的愿景。

虽然第一长夜与秋分相关，但在节日前一两周便开始预热庆祝也并不罕见。这种做法根植于本地对天书宗教根源的改造；自帝皇自仪兴时期以来，@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QZD0u1jxwz0kj8uI]{法拉斯玛}与@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog18sangpo]{桑博齐}的信徒，原本便会在初秋的不同日子里祭奠亡者，并与自身终有一死的命运和解。

在柳岸镇中...

请注意，本文的大部分内容都在探讨现代的第一长夜节日是什么样子。在“第二幕：落叶任飘零”期间，络新妇统治逾一个世纪所带来的影响，并不像后来那样深刻左右这一节日传统的发展。本冒险也包含建议，说明这些变化可能会如何影响部分庆典与传统——特别是在那些并不存在络新妇统治115年这一前提的情况下。

第一长夜是一个极具身体性的节日，甚至在节日当天到来之前便已如此。随着期待不断升温，本地人会更加卖力而欢快地劳作，希望提前完成各种职责，好腾出时间为节日做准备；他们伴随着嘹亮的民歌节奏工作，而歌词与韵律中往往蕴含着传统农业技艺或本地传说的见解。秋日清冽的微风中，飘散着木烟熏制的腌肉与熬炼油脂的气味；与此同时，为临时节庆场地施工的声响会一直持续到夜里很晚。万物都鲜活、喧闹而充满乐趣，而在闹鬼的神门，每个人都比平时更有精神。搏动的汗水与流淌的鲜血、歌声、以及与季节更迭赛跑的一切……都旨在提醒生者与死者，生命有多么顽强——无论那是仍在活着的生命，还是只存在于精魂记忆中的生命。

尽管琅罗伊及其党羽这些占领者自以为已牢牢扼住这片受蜘蛛诅咒的神门之地，第一长夜仍呈现出一种安静的反抗；人们会想起为自己而活意味着什么，也会想起这又多么常常需要人们共同承诺彼此尊重与求生。这些细小的颠覆会引向更大胆的举动；为了在没有官方支援的情况下熬过闹鬼的冬季，即便是最循规蹈矩的居民，也愿意违反络新妇占领者的法令，去寻找云游四方的驱邪师、土匪军火贩子与流浪佣兵，以获得武器或解决办法，来克服寒冷季节中亡灵带来的威胁。虽然神门的络新妇通常会将这类彰显或积聚力量的行为视为叛国，并以极其痛苦的死亡加以惩罚，但出于只有她们自己知晓的原因，她们通常不会在第一长夜前后执行这类惩罚。

First Long Night

As autumn’s days yield to the burgeoning night, those who dwell in Shenmen’s countryside begin preparations for winter. These preparations are organized around rural families’ observation of First Long Night, an evening spent together in solemn commemorations of deceased kin as well as witnessing the community’s hopeful aspirations.

While First Long Night speaks to the autumn equinox, it isn’t uncommon for pre-festivities to begin a fortnight or two before. Such a practice has its roots in local adaptations of Tian-Shu religious traditions; since the imperial Yixing, adherents of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QZD0u1jxwz0kj8uI]{Pharasma} and @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog18sangpo]{Sangpotshi} originally set various dates in early autumn for paying respects to the dead and making peace with one’s mortality.

In Willowshore...

Note that much of this article explores how the festival of First Long Night exists in the modern day. During “Act 2: Let the Leaves Fall,” the impact of over a century of rule under the jorogumo isn’t as much a factor in how the festival’s traditions have grown. The adventure includes advice on how these changes might affect some of the celebrations and traditions where the lack of 115 years of jorogumo rule wouldn’t apply.

First Long Night is a very physical event, even before the date of the festival arrives. As anticipation builds, locals work more exuberantly in hopes of getting ahead of duties so as to have time to prepare for the festival, working to the tempo of resonant folk songs with the lyrics and cadence often containing insights into traditional farming techniques or local legends. Fall’s crisp breeze carries the scent of wood-smoked preserved meat and rendered lard as townsfolk prepare food stores, while the noise of construction for temporary festival grounds goes on well into the evening. Everything is vivid, loud, and fun, and everyone is a little more spirited than usual in ghost-haunted Shenmen. The pulsing sweat and pouring blood, the songs, the race to beat the turn of seasons... all intended to remind both the living and dead of the tenacity of life—be it a life still being lived or one that exists only in a spirit’s memory.

Even though the occupying forces of Lang Loi and her cronies think they have a stranglehold on spider-cursed Shenmen, First Long Night presents a quiet defiance, as people remember what it means to live for themselves and how often that requires shared commitments to mutual respect and survival. These tiny subversions lead to bolder ones; to survive haunted winters without official support, even the most law-abiding residents are willing to break the jorogumo occupiers’ laws to seek itinerant exorcists, bandit arms dealers, and wandering mercenaries to provide weapons or solutions to overcome the cold season’s undead threats. While the jorogumo of Shenmen normally consider these acts of asserting or accumulating power treasonous and punishable with excruciating death, for reasons known only to themselves, they don’t generally enforce such punishments near First Long Night.
