Player Character Options.name: 玩家角色选项 Player Character Options
Player Character Options.text:
玩家角色选项

遵循桑博齐之道，或研习载有桑博齐秘密的文本与学识（例如丹杉寺的 @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog09inther.JournalEntryPage.09e11hiddenlib00]{藏匿的图书馆} 中的那些内容）的玩家角色，可获得这些罕见玩家角色选项的许可。

Player Character Options

A PC who follows the ways of Sangpotshi or studies texts and lore containing Sangpotshi secrets (such as those found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog09inther.JournalEntryPage.09e11hiddenlib00]{Hidden Library} of the Tan Sugi Monastery) gains access to these uncommon player character options.

Nindorus.name: 宁多鲁斯 Nindorus
Nindorus.text:
宁多鲁斯

宁多鲁斯是轮回与桑博齐哲学最强大的敌人之一。面向游戏主持的宁多鲁斯讨论始于@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog19cycles]{Here}，而各个具体的宁多鲁斯则出现在@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia]{Bestiary}中。玩家角色可以像对待任何生物一样，通过回忆知识来了解单个宁多鲁斯的更多信息；但若想进一步了解这些相对鲜为人知的怪物，则可以尝试进行一次@Check[nindoru-lore|dc:15|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge]、@Check[religion|dc:20|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge]或@Check[occultism|dc:20|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge]检定来回忆知识。成功会揭示此处给出的通俗常识，而大成功还会揭示更深层的知识。

成功—通俗常识：这些邪魔有许多不同形态，但其中许多个体都具有可辨识的特征，例如细长而破损的肢体、被篮子或笼子困住或替代的头、渗出血红色蝴蝶云团的伤口，或是使用被阴邪力量维系在一起的破损武器与工具。腐化在它们体内根深蒂固，以至于它们对失去之物的渴求变得扭曲，最终显现为对转世的灵魂的贪食欲望，凌驾于一切其他欲望之上。

大成功—更深层知识：这些邪魔能够放大自身自私的想法，将其显现为只服务于它们的物体，甚至仆从。最强大的个体甚至能仅凭思想就显现出整个社会或领域。宁多鲁斯将这些造物视作珍贵财产，但一旦它们被摧毁，便立刻将其遗忘。一些学者认为，这种行为是在嘲弄轮回，将个体的一生与邪魔工具那转瞬即逝的存在相提并论。这类推测源于宁多鲁斯表现得如同桑博齐秘修士的毁灭性对立面。它们可以使用类似的异能法术体系，而且往往潜伏于神殿，以及自然与文明之间的边界——这些也正是桑博齐秘修士经常巡守的地方。批评这些理论的人指出，那些地点同样也是宁多鲁斯能找到其偏好猎物之处，并坚持认为驱使宁多鲁斯的是低等本能，从而否定它们具有任何组织性目的的说法。

Nindorus

Nindorus are among the greatest enemies of reincarnation and the Sangpotshi philosophy. A GM-facing discussion on nindorus begins @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog19cycles]{Here}, while individual nindorus appear in the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia]{Bestiary}. A PC can learn more about individual nindorus by Recalling Knowledge as with any creature, but one who wishes to know more about these relatively obscure monsters can attempt a @Check[nindoru-lore|dc:15|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[religion|dc:20|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[occultism|dc:20|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge. A success reveals the common knowledge given here, and a critical success also revels the deeper knowledge as well.

Success—Common Knowledge: These fiends take many forms, but many share identifiable traits, such as long broken limbs, heads trapped or replaced by baskets or cages, wounds that seep clouds of blood-red butterflies, or the utilization of broken weapons and tools held together by sinister forces. Corruption runs so deep within them that their yearning for what they’ve lost becomes twisted, manifesting as an appetite for reincarnated souls above all others.

Critical Success—Deeper Knowledge: These fiends can amplify their selfish thoughts to manifest objects or even minions that serve them alone. The most powerful can manifest entire societies or realms from only their thoughts. Nindorus treat these creations as prized possessions but forget about them as soon as they’re destroyed. Some scholars see this behavior as a mockery of reincarnation, drawing a parallel between an individual’s life and the ephemeral existence of a fiend’s tool. Such speculation comes from nindorus behaving as the destructive opposites of Sangpotshi mystics. They have access to similar repertoires of occult spells, and they tend to stalk temples and boundaries between nature and civilization—the same places Sangpotshi mystics often patrol. Critics of such theories point out that those locations are also where nindorus can find their preferred prey and insist that base instincts drive nindorus, dismissing the notion that they have any organized purpose.

Cycles of Life.name: 生命轮回 Cycles of Life
Cycles of Life.text:
生命轮回

桑博齐以长远的眼光看待生命。其典籍描述了映照生、死与重生的循环——文明的兴衰、灾害后自然的复苏，以及人们在面对变化时会重新依赖的熟悉行为模式。

有些循环具有建设性，应当加以保留；但另一些则会延续苦难，而这未必是个人力量所能打破的。即便是负面的循环，也能帮助灵魂朝向最终的启迪而成长，持续经济困境所带来的艰难便是其中一例。尽管如此，追随桑博齐的人一致认为，贫困毫无疑问会造成巨大的痛苦，应当加以对抗。与此同时，命运决定了不同的行为与信念会导向不平等的结果。善解的信徒会尽其所能对抗不平等，同时也接受人必须与其存在这一现实共处。他们鼓励那些哀叹自身处境的人审视自己能从经历中学到什么。这种自省能够带来启迪与改变。如果每个人都善待彼此，他们最终或许能够消除贫困。桑博齐的准则帮助信徒培育正向循环，并摆脱或对抗负向循环。

信徒们也谨慎地保护自然世界与城市世界之间的平衡。他们认为所有活着的生物都走在同一条道路上，并以自己也希望得到的尊严来对待它们。帮助他人是一项使命，不过他们也会谨慎选择帮助的方式，使他人能够学习与成长，而非依赖外来的协助。他们提倡可持续的生活方式，只取所需，并尽可能将伤害降到最低。这样的选择旨在保全现有循环，使后代也能得到与先人相同的机会。这种保存并提升万物的愿望意味着，暴力是最后手段，但并非禁忌。破坏性的力量试图腐化转生轮回，而桑博齐的信徒会动用一切手段守护生命之河。

Cycles of Life

Sangpotshi takes a long view on life. Its texts describe cycles that mirror life, death, and rebirth—the rise and fall of civilizations, the renewal of nature after a disaster, and the familiar behaviors people fall back on when confronted with change.

Some cycles are constructive and should be preserved, but others perpetuate suffering that might not be within the power of individuals to break. Even negative cycles can help souls grow toward eventual enlightenment, with the difficulties that arise from constant economic peril being one such example. Nonetheless, those who follow Sangpotshi agree that, without a doubt, poverty causes immense suffering and should be counteracted. At the same time, fate dictates that different behaviors and beliefs lead to unequal outcomes. Followers of Sangpotshi do what lies within their power to combat inequality while accepting that one must live with the reality of its existence. They encourage those who lament their situation to examine what they can learn from their experiences. This introspection can lead to enlightenment and change. If everyone treats each other well, they might eventually eliminate poverty. Sangpotshi’s guidelines help followers nurture positive cycles and escape or counter negative ones.

Followers are also careful to protect the balance between the natural and urbanized worlds. They see all living creatures as on the same path and treat them with the dignity they would want to receive in turn. Helping others is a duty, though they’re careful to assist in ways that allow others to learn and grow rather than become reliant on external aid. They promote sustainable methods of living, taking only what one needs and in ways that minimize harm. Such choices aim to preserve existing cycles so that future generations have access to the same opportunities that past ones did. This desire to preserve and uplift means that violence is a last resort, but it isn’t anathema. Destructive forces seek to corrupt the cycle of reincarnation, and Sangpotshi followers defend the River of Life through all means at their disposal.

Past Life Curiosity.name: 好奇前世 Past Life Curiosity
Past Life Curiosity.text:
好奇前世

那么，为什么会有人想要了解自己的过去呢？也许有人觉得自己处境不公，再也无法忍受。比如一个在专横老板手下工作的雇员。这样的人可能会去寻找一位秘修者，询问老板这样压迫自己，是否是因为他们前世做过什么事。答案可能是否定的，那么这名雇员也许就会觉得自己可以安心离开当前处境，去寻找更好的工作环境。

如果答案是肯定的，这名雇员可能会因知道自己的痛苦有其意义而感到安慰，并选择留下来，以了结自己的灵性债务。如果他们离开，未来可能又会在这位老板手下工作；更糟的是，在来世还可能与对方产生关系，到那时他们就没法这么轻易摆脱这笔债了。也许秘修者看见，他们的困境只会再持续一年；如果他们熬过这段时间，他们与老板的关系就会改善，或者老板会离开。秘修者也可能看见另一种偿还债务的方法，比如告诉他们老板为何如此愤怒，让这个人能够直面老板，直接解决他们之间的问题。秘修者会在担心无知会导致糟糕后果时，分享某人前世的细节。

Past Life Curiosity

So why would anyone ever want to know about their past? Perhaps someone feels they’re in an unjust situation and can’t tolerate it any longer. Take the example of a worker under an oppressive boss. Such a person might seek out a mystic and ask if the boss oppresses them because of something they did in a past life. The answer might be no, in which case the worker might feel free to leave their situation to find a better working environment.

If the answer is yes, the worker might find comfort in knowing their suffering has a purpose and stay so that they can end their spiritual debt. If they leave, they could find themselves working under the boss again in the future or, worse, become related to them in a future life where they can’t escape their debt so easily. Perhaps the mystic sees that their troubles will only last another year, and if they wait it out, their relationship with their boss will improve or the boss will leave. The mystic might also see another way to resolve the debt, such as telling them why their boss is so angry, enabling the person to confront their boss and resolve their problems directly. Mystics share details about someone’s past life when they fear that ignorance will result in a bad outcome.

Spiritual Connections.name: 精魂结缘 Spiritual Connections
Spiritual Connections.text:
精魂结缘

在天夏，人们有时会在生活中遭遇困难时去寻求桑博齐秘修者的帮助，以了解这些困难是否源于某种精魂结缘。这类关系中的某些类型十分常见，在大多数天夏文化中都属于通俗常识。人们往往会再次遭遇那些在自己前世中对自己产生过影响的人。

同缘之系源于前世中建立了强烈联系的人，不过这种联系的性质各不相同。他们可能曾是家人、挚友，或志同道合的同伴，比如一同耕种公地的农夫，或在同一支战团中作战的士兵。这些关系可能是吉利的，也可能是对立的。两位在前世始终彼此照料的朋友，如今可能会以配偶或亲子关系形成一段吉利的联系。而同样的关系也可能因灵性债务而变得对立。也许某个骗子骗走了他人的一生积蓄，导致对方早逝——这种关系在来生中，便可能显现为会造成重大财务损失的配偶或子女。这种损失可能是蓄意为之，例如偷窃；也可能是间接造成的，例如健康危机所致。

秘修者会谨慎地告诫人们，不要把灵性关系当作合理化怨恨的借口，也不要对存在哪些灵性纽带妄下断言。回到前面那个对立关系的例子，偷窃的配偶可能是在潜意识中为前世的失窃复仇，也可能只是在开启一轮此前并不存在的愤怒与怨怼循环。

友谊既可能是新关系的开端，也可能是较弱灵性纽带的再现。短暂的友谊或许是由于前世的一道单一灵性纽带，一旦了结，灵魂便各自分离。也许在前世，两个陌生人曾向某人伸出援手。来世中，他们成了那位曾被他们帮助过的灵魂门下的同窗伙伴；而当他们习得实现理想职业所需的技能后，彼此便渐渐疏远。

好的命运能改善一个人出生时的处境。前世中的伟大英雄，可能会因为从许多其他灵魂那里积累了善意，而在来生出生于富裕之家。不过，过去并不决定未来，桑博齐告诫人们，应当依据他人的行为而非地位来尊重他人。一个富有的继承人也可能在新生中变得残忍而贪婪，因为他们缺乏对他人的同理心。

桑博齐的追随者相信，有些降生于糟糕处境中的情况源于命运，但他们同样警告说，作出这种假设是危险的。一些强大的秘修者会选择转生到艰难的环境中，因为这可能使他们的力量更快显现。另一些接近成为桑钵的灵魂则会立下自我牺牲的誓言，选择承受厄运，以防其落到无辜的灵魂身上。灵魂被分配进入新躯体一事，在许多方面都无法知晓。坠落的分支无法选择自己会被冲到哪一处岸边，正如生命之河中的灵魂也无法选择自己会在哪里重入生命。命运或许能提高一个人出生于某些处境之中的几率，或提高其一生中遭遇特定事件的可能性，但它从不保证这些事情必然发生。

一个人如何回应自己当下的处境，才是桑博齐与命运中最重要的性相。应以谦逊接受好运，以积极的态度面对困境。桑博齐教导人们，应在可能的时候行善，保持良好的判断力，并依循“以己所欲，施于人”的准则生活。

Spiritual Connections

People in Tian Xia sometimes seek out a Sangpotshi mystic when they encounter difficulties in their life to learn if those difficulties are the result of a spiritual connection. Some types of these relationships occur frequently and are common knowledge in most Tian Xia cultures. Individuals tend to encounter the same people who impacted them in prior incarnations.

Kindred ties arise from those who developed strong connections in previous lives, though the nature of those connections varies. They might have been family, close friends, or compatriots, such as farmers working communal land together or soldiers fighting in the same war band. These relationships can be propitious or antagonistic. Two friends who took care of each other throughout a previous life could now have a propitious relationship as spouses or parent and child. Those same relationships can also be antagonistic due to a spiritual debt. Perhaps a con artist stole someone’s life savings, causing their premature death—that relationship can manifest in the next life as a spouse or child who causes great financial loss. Such a loss can be deliberate, such as through theft, or indirect, such as due to a health crisis.

Mystics are careful to warn people not to use spiritual relationships as an excuse to justify resentment, nor to make assumptions about what spiritual bonds exist. Going back to the previous antagonistic example, a spouse who steals could be subconsciously taking revenge for a theft in a previous life, or they could be starting a new cycle of anger and resentment where none existed before.

Friendships can be the start of new relationships or the recurrence of weaker spiritual bonds. Ephemeral friendships might be due to a single spiritual bond from a previous life that results in the souls parting once resolved. Perhaps two strangers came to someone’s aid in a previous life. They become study partners in their next life under the tutelage of the soul they helped, and when they learn the skills they need to attain their dream jobs, they then drift apart.

A good destiny can improve one’s position at birth. A great hero from a previous life might be born into a wealthy family in the next because of the good will they incurred from many other souls. The past doesn’t dictate the future, though, and Sangpotshi warns that you should respect people for their behavior, not their status. A wealthy heir could become cruel and greedy in their new life because they lack empathy for others.

Sangpotshi followers believe some births into bad situations result from fate, but they again warn that it’s dangerous to make such assumptions. Some powerful mystics choose to reincarnate into difficult circumstances because it can cause their powers to manifest more quickly. Other souls that are close to becoming Sangpots take oaths of self-sacrifice, choosing to suffer ill fortune to prevent it from falling on innocent souls. The assignment of souls into new bodies is unknowable in many respects. A fallen branch can choose where it washes ashore no more than a soul in the River of Life chooses where it reenters life. Fate can improve one’s odds of being born into certain circumstances or encountering specific events in one’s life, but it never guarantees such occurrences.

How one responds to their current situation is the most important aspect of Sangpotshi and fate. Receive good fortune with humility and face trouble with a positive attitude. Sangpotshi tells people to do good whenever possible, exercise good judgment, and live by the rule of treating others as you would want others to treat you.

The Nature of Reincarnation.name: 轮回的本质 The Nature of Reincarnation
The Nature of Reincarnation.text:
轮回的本质

关于哪些因素决定转生灵魂的际遇，众说纷纭，而其中最流行的思想流派以“道”的形式存在，各自有着独特的实践方式。天道源自起源于伏陀罗的哲学家波阇潘迪尼的教导；他认为神祇会审判凡人如何度过一生，并决定他们来世的地位。

地道的信奉者认为，命运是一种自然现象。行动会在单独一生之内产生可观察到的后果，因此合乎逻辑的结论是，命运在多次生命之间也遵循同样的规则。人们如何彼此相待，才是最重要的。

行者之道是最后一个主要实践流派。与其专注于哲学追求，行者之道更鼓励以身体力行的方式去探索存在的本质。这一道的信徒将那些同名的桑钵视作榜样；这些开悟之人对宇宙获得了如此深刻的理解，以至于与之融为一体。

有些人认为，轮回的真正本质存在于这些不同信念之间的某处。一个灵魂的命运与归宿，并不是一种可以量化衡量的力量，就像人无法衡量世间善意或苦难的总量一样。相反，最适合将其想象为一本本个人账本，任何人都可以在其中写下一笔。神祇的忠诚仆役可能会从一位神圣代表那里得到一条正面记录；受害者则可能在加害者的账本上记下一笔债务；而一个因自身行动而深感愧疚的罪犯，甚至可能在社会和受害者都已原谅他之后很久，仍在自己的账本上记下一条过失。至于这些记录是否会被执行，也取决于提交它们的人自己，因为并不存在某个客观的外在者来强制实施这些裁决。它不过是人们相信自己彼此之间以及对自己所亏欠的一切之总和，以及他们依照这些信念付诸行动的动机有多强。

这种信念或许正是让相信轮回的人能够选择再次出生的力量。历史上最伟大的英雄与恶徒，都是那些完成了他们相信自己必须完成之事的人。从这个意义上说，命运是可塑的，而每一道都能找到充分证据来印证其教义。每一道中最强大的祭司与秘法修行者都宣称，自己能够看见一个人在其所有生世中与他人积累下来的命定联系。他们沿着那些线索去理解行为模式，以及人与人之间清算循环的规律。他们的知识使他们能够辨明人内心最深的渴望，仲裁灵魂之间的争端，并要求立即进行命定的清算。

桑博齐的另一条关键教义，是恪守节制。桑博齐的最终目标，是成为理想版本的自己，并超越凡俗苦难。桑博齐的秘法修行者教导说，苦难源于欲望。他们并不评判个人欲望究竟是好是坏，但他们指出，欲望会制造对凡俗世界的执著，而这会导致灵魂停滞并受苦。举例来说，一个人若痴迷于某个目标，一旦无法实现，便会变得不快乐。他们可能会追逐那个目标，以至于损害自己生活中的其他方面。反过来，一个实现了欲望的人，也可能会害怕失去自己已获得之物，于是专注于维持现状，而不是满足于自己已经拥有的一切。

拒斥欲望，并不意味着放弃人生目标或社会责任。桑博齐并不赞同那些为了避免执著而抛弃自身义务的人，认为那本身也是一种极端；不过，若这样做不会伤害他人，信徒有时也会选择暂时放下自己的处境。相反，这一哲学提供的是关于如何在自身处境中好好生活、并清偿自身灵性账目的指引。这种指引也包括不要过于深究前世。桑博齐的大多数信徒都认为，大多数人——轮回裔除外——不记得前世，是有原因的。他们明白，重生给予他们一个机会，让他们能把账目一笔勾销，摆脱那些已走到尽头或变得不健康的执著。桑博齐的秘法修行者珍视自己获取前世化身信息的能力，但也谨慎地适度使用它。只有当他们认为过去与某个正在当下折磨某人的问题有关时，他们才会稍稍窥视往昔。

The Nature of Reincarnation

Theories abound about what factors determine the lot of a reincarnated soul, and the most popular schools of thought exist as “paths,” each with unique practices. The Heavens Path originates from the teachings of Vudrani philosopher Bhoja Pandiri, who believed gods judge how mortals lived and assign their station in their next life.

Adherents of the Earthly Path believe fate is a natural occurrence. Actions have observable consequences within a single lifetime, so the logical conclusion is fate follows the same rules across multiple lifetimes. How people treat each other is what matters most.

The Traveler’s Path is the final major practice. Rather than focus on philosophical pursuits, the Traveler’s Path encourages the physical act of exploring the nature of existence. Adherents of this path find role models in the eponymous Sangpots, enlightened individuals who gained such a profound understanding of the universe that they merged with it.

Some believe that the true nature of reincarnation lies somewhere between these various beliefs. A soul’s fate and destiny isn’t a quantifiable force that can be measured any more than one can measure the total amount of good will or suffering in existence. It can instead be best imagined as individual ledgers in which anyone can write an entry. The faithful servant of a deity might receive a positive entry from a divine representative, while a victim might place a debt on the ledger of their aggressor, and a criminal who feels intense guilt for their actions might leave a demerit on themselves long after society and their victims have forgiven them. It’s also up to those submitting entries to act on them, for there’s no objective outsider enforcing these judgments. It’s simply the sum of what people believe they owe each other and themselves, and the extent of their motivation to act on those beliefs.

Such convictions might be the force that allows those who believe in reincarnation to choose to be born anew. The greatest heroes and villains throughout history are those who accomplished what they believed they must do. In that sense, fate is malleable, and each path can find substantial evidence to validate its teachings. The most powerful priests and mystics of every path claim to be able to see the fated connections an individual has accumulated with others all of their lifetimes. They follow those threads to understand patterns of behavior and cycles of reckoning between people. Their knowledge enables them to identify people’s deepest desires, arbitrate disputes between souls, and demand immediate fateful reckoning.

Another key tenet of Sangpotshi is adherence to moderation. The end goal of Sangpotshi is to become an ideal version of oneself and to transcend mortal suffering. Sangpotshi mystics teach that suffering comes from desire. They don’t pass judgment on whether individual desires are good or bad, but they point out that desires create attachments to the mortal realm that cause souls to stagnate and suffer. Someone who becomes obsessed with a goal, for example, becomes unhappy if they can’t accomplish it. They might pursue their goal to the detriment of other aspects of their life. Alternatively, someone who achieves a desire might fear losing what they’ve acquired, focusing on preserving the status quo instead of being satisfied with what they possess.

Spurning desire doesn’t mean abandoning life goals or societal responsibilities. Sangpotshi frowns on those who abandon their obligations to avoid attachments, viewing that as its own extreme, though followers sometimes choose to set aside their circumstances if doing so doesn’t harm others. The philosophy instead provides guidance on how to live well within one’s circumstances and settle one’s spiritual accounts. That guidance includes not diving too deeply into past lives. Most followers of Sangpotshi believe there’s a reason most people—samsarans excluded—don’t remember their previous lives. They understand that rebirth gives them an opportunity to wipe their slate clean and shed attachments that have run their course or become unhealthy. Sangpotshi mystics prize their ability to access information about prior incarnations but are careful to use it in moderation. They only peek into the past when they believe it’s relevant to a problem plaguing someone in the present.

Sangpotshi.name: 桑博齐 Sangpotshi
Sangpotshi.text:
桑博齐

对轮回循环的信仰在天夏各地都很普遍，而@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.WfqLY2Fm1LGCcG5X]{桑博齐}则是阐释轮回如何运作、以及它服务于何种目的的核心哲学。大多数追随者并不认为桑博齐是一种与现有神祇崇拜相竞争的信念，而是将其视为对这些信仰的补充。这一哲学关注的是如何过好凡人的一生。有些人对这种实践持怀疑态度，认为这是试图“欺骗”死后世界的常规秩序，但天夏神祇及其追随者则有不同看法。毕竟，轮回与灵魂可能面对的任何其他裁决一样，都是正当有效的。桑博齐教导追随者，轮回是一种对信念的磨炼，因为每一世都既会带来偏离自身信条的种种时刻，也会带来自我提升的许多机会。

桑博齐也被称为生命之河。这个名字并非比喻——它描述的是与灵魂之河相对应的一条河流；灵魂之河将死者的灵魂送往@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QZD0u1jxwz0kj8uI]{法拉斯玛}的骨园。相信轮回的人教导说，这些灵魂会转而进入生命之河，其水流会一次又一次地将灵魂送回凡间，直到它们命中注定不再继续这重生循环为止。跨越所有人生、由各类已行之动作累积而成的结果，会决定一个灵魂下一世所处的境遇。天夏神祇、祂们的代理者以及志同道合的盟友，会保护生命之河，抵御那些企图趁灵魂在途中时加以掠食的破坏性力量，但他们并不总能成功。超自然操弄的影响，或是不死生物污染的玷污，都可能将灵魂从轮回循环中撕扯出去，把它转化为宁多鲁——一种具毁灭性的邪魔，意图扰乱轮回循环，并通过将灵魂从通往启悟的道路上引向腐化与残酷，来摧毁凡人生命留下的恒久功业。

Sangpotshi

Faith in the cycle of reincarnation is widespread across Tian Xia, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.WfqLY2Fm1LGCcG5X]{Sangpotshi} is the organizing philosophy around how reincarnation works and what purpose it serves. Most followers don’t see Sangpotshi as a belief that competes with worship of existing gods, but rather complements these faiths. The philosophy focuses on how to live a mortal life well. Some are skeptical about the practice, seeing it as an attempt to “cheat” the regular order of the afterlife, but Tian deities and their followers hold a different perspective. After all, reincarnation is as valid a judgment as any that a soul might face. Sangpotshi teaches followers that reincarnation is an exercise in conviction, for each life presents as many occasions to stray from one’s tenets as it does opportunities to improve oneself.

Sangpotshi is also known as the River of Life. The name isn’t metaphorical—it describes a parallel to the River of Souls, which carries the souls of the dead to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QZD0u1jxwz0kj8uI]{Pharasma}’s Boneyard. Those who believe in reincarnation teach that these souls enter the River of Life instead, whose currents carry souls back to mortal life as many times as they’re destined to continue the cycle of rebirth. The cumulative effects of lived actions across all lives determine the circumstances of a soul’s next life. Tian deities, their representatives, and like-minded allies protect the River of Life from disruptive forces who would prey on souls in transit, but they don’t always succeed. The influence of supernatural manipulation or the taint of undeath can tear a soul from the cycle of reincarnation, transforming it into a nindoru—a destructive category of fiend that seeks to disrupt the cycle of reincarnation and to destroy the lasting works of mortal life by diverting a soul from its path to enlightenment into corruption and cruelty.

Cycles of Destruction.name: 毁灭轮回 Cycles of Destruction

Nindorus in the World.name: 世界中的灵堕魔 Nindorus in the World
Nindorus in the World.text:
世界中的灵堕魔

与其他邪魔相比，宁多鲁斯在格拉利昂的存在相对罕见，且活动范围有限。它们起源于天夏，这一点迄今为止也基本将其影响限制在这片大陆上。以下地点是宁多鲁活动尤为显著的地区。

楚业：这个由恶鬼统治的国度中弥漫的残酷，对宁多鲁斯颇具吸引力；楚业栖息着数个大型灵煞，它们与恒将军的代理人合作，镇压任何叛乱的迹象。这些合作关系很可能是因双方共同崇拜@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.6O4UGWcYERDEugzk]{同时也越发崇拜文业王}而促成的，同时，恶鬼作为堕落神使而诞生，与宁多鲁源于受腐化的凡人灵魂，这两者之间也有相似之处。

神门：神门阴郁荒凉的地带是宁多鲁斯理想的狩猎场，它们沉醉于这个国家人民的苦难之中。由于神门大多由分散各处的村庄构成，人口失踪不幸地极为常见，这些邪魔常常在一个个社区之间迅速流窜，缓慢地猎杀当地居民。苦迦菩提在此统领着许多追随者，他们都在等待主人挣脱束缚的那一天。

天京：喜好吞食受神明沾染之灵魂的宁多鲁斯，会将天京当作自己的巢穴；它们乐于见到异界入侵与匪徒占地为王，使这片土地因创伤而变得格外“甘美”。天京的神子之森中那些被腐坏侵蚀的区域，是许多灵煞的藏身处，而研究者推测，当地对西格克的崇敬，可能与邪魔腐化有关。

紫霞：受其对轮回裔长久以来的仇恨驱使，宁多鲁斯若有机会，便会成千上万地涌入紫霞。多山的地形和善德勇的防御基本阻挡了它们的实体入侵，但崇拜穆萨加尼的宁多鲁斯仍经常试图重现那位苦修者的入侵，并在搜寻通往觉峰核心地带的地下路线。

Nindorus in the World

Compared to other fiends, nindorus are relatively rare and limited in their presence in Golarion. Their origins in Tian Xia have largely kept their influence to this continent so far. The following locations are notable sites of nindoru activity.

Chu Ye: The cruelty in this oni-ruled kingdom appeals to nindorus, and Chu Ye is home to several large ninsats that work with the agents of Shogun Tsuneni to quell any signs of rebellion. These partnerships are likely fostered due to a shared worship of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.6O4UGWcYERDEugzk]{Fumeiyoshi}, as well as similarities between an oni’s genesis as a corrupted kami and a nindoru’s source being from a corrupted mortal soul.

Shenmen: The dreary reaches of Shenmen are ideal hunting grounds for nindorus, who relish the misery of the nation’s citizenry. Since Shenmen is largely composed of spread-out villages where missing persons are unfortunately commonplace, these fiends often dart from community to community, slowly picking off locals. Kugaptee commands many followers here, all waiting for the day that their master breaks free.

Tianjing: Nindorus who enjoy feeding on god-touched souls make their home in Tianjing, relishing the extraplanar incursions and bandit takeovers that have made the land sweet with trauma. The blighted portions of Tianjing’s Kaimuko Wood are a hideout for many ninsats, and researchers speculate that the local veneration of Sigek may be tied to fiendish corruption.

Zi Ha: Fueled by their long-standing hatred of samsarans, nindorus would rush into Zi Ha by the thousands if they could. The mountainous terrain and Sangpo-Jong’s defenses largely keep physical incursions at bay, but nindorus who worship Musagani frequently attempt to replicate the Ascetic’s invasion and are searching for underground routes into the very heart of the Enlightened Peaks.

Sigek.name: 西格克 Sigek
Sigek.text:
西格克

与西格克以宁多鲁苦修者身份回归有关的证据，直到帝国纪年7214年才刚刚被发现；当时一群开拓者击败了三个以天京轮回裔社群为目标的灵煞。每个灵煞都有一处巢穴，里面数十具尸体环绕着蓝色雕像摆放；那些雕像看起来像是有着人类面部特征、多口的宁多鲁。开拓者抵达时，这些宁多鲁斯正陷入狂乱，并死战到底，反复高喊着“西格克将重获新生！”所有雕像都被运送到过峡的天灯会馆，自那以后一直被锁藏保管至今。

禁忌 治愈他人的寄生感染，维持一段联盟超过一年，使一个非宁多鲁生物死而复生

Sigek

Evidence related to Sigek’s return as a nindoru Ascetic was only recently discovered in 7214 ic, when a group of Pathfinders defeated three ninsats targeting samsaran communities in Tianjing. Each ninsat had a lair where dozens of corpses were placed around blue statues that resembled a multi-mawed nindoru with human facial features. The nindorus were in a frenzy when the Pathfinders arrived and fought to the death while repeatedly chanting the phrase “Sigek will be born again!” All the statues were transported to Goka’s Lantern Lodge, where they remain under lock and key to this day.

Musagani.name: 穆萨加尼 Musagani
Musagani.text:
穆萨加尼

庞大的穆萨加尼是所有已知灵堕魔中体型最大的个体。帝国纪年6778年，它率领一支灵煞渗透紫霞国，在此期间造成了数百人遇害，最终死于白骨与杜松之城的巨人之手。在这次放逐之前，穆萨加尼吸收了66名巨人的灵魂，膨胀至巨兽般的体量，自那之后的数个世纪里，再没有任何宁多鲁达到过这样的规模。

典范 扰乱组织、杀死比你更大的生物、阻止复活或转世

Musagani

Immense Musagani, the largest of all known nindorus, led a ninsat that infiltrated the nation of Zi Ha in 6778 ic, during which Musagani claimed hundreds of victims before finally meeting an end at the hands of the City of Bone and Juniper’s giants. Prior to this banishment, Musagani absorbed the souls of 66 giants, swelling to behemoth proportions that no nindoru has replicated in the centuries since.

Kugaptee.name: 苦迦菩提 Kugaptee
Kugaptee.text:
苦迦菩提

苦迦菩提是过去一千年间最令人畏惧的宁多鲁斯之一。据说他有四个头和四只手臂，分别象征一年中的四季。6223 ic，英雄谭隋靖终结了他对天夏中部一片偏远地区的统治，尽管她也在击败他的同一场战斗中牺牲。她的灵魂转生为一棵巨大的杉树，生长在苦迦菩提之墓上方；只要这棵树仍然存在，这个死去的邪魔就永远无法转生并重返这个世界。

关注领域 诅咒、被玷污的坟墓、闹鬼的荒野，以及季节性灾害

典范 诅咒活着的生物，亵渎墓地与田园自然地区，

禁忌 举行意在让死者安息的埋葬仪式，移除除自己之外任何人身上的诅咒，让非宁多鲁生物复活

Kugaptee

Kugaptee was one of the most formidable nindorus of the last millennium. Said to have four heads and four arms, each representing one of the seasons of the year, his reign over a remote reach of central Tian Xia was brought to an end in 6223 ic by the heroine Tan Sui-Jing, although she perished in the same battle where she defeated him. Her soul, reincarnated as an immense sugi tree, grows above Kugaptee’s grave, ensuring the dead fiend will never reincarnate and return to this world while the tree remains.

Nindoru Ascetics.name: 灵堕魔苦行者 Nindoru Ascetics
Nindoru Ascetics.text:
灵堕魔苦行者

在宁多鲁斯之中，还存在着更为危险、能够运用神圣力量的存在。这些宁多鲁半神统称为苦修者，由于太过隐秘，尚未建立起任何广泛传播的信仰，因此整体上仍是个谜。最为人所知的三位苦修者本身也是谜团，在现代社会中大多已被遗忘。然而在他们活跃的地区，他们的存在却不容忽视。

灵堕魔苦行者的牧师极其罕见，但他们确实存在——通常是以孤身狂热者，或非牧师宁多鲁教团领袖的身份出现。不过，随着时代推移，灵堕魔苦行者的信仰也有可能逐渐壮大，尤其是如果你的肆季鬼志战役以灾害告终，而苦迦菩提重返生者世界的话！

Nindoru Ascetics

There exists among nindorus much more dangerous entities wielding divine powers. Obscure enough to not have established any widespread faiths, these nindoru demigods, known collectively as the Ascetics, are largely a mystery. The three most well-known Ascetics are themselves enigmas largely forgotten by modern society. Yet in the regions where they’re active, their presence can’t be ignored.

Clerics of nindoru ascetics are incredibly rare, but they do exist—typically in the role of lone fanatics or leaders of non-cleric nindoru cults. Over time, though, it’s possible for a nindoru ascetic’s faith to potentially grow larger, particularly if the events of your Season of Ghosts campaign end in disaster and Kugaptee returns to the living world!

About Nindorus.name: 关于灵堕魔 About Nindorus
About Nindorus.text:
关于灵堕魔

尽管毫无疑问还存在种类更广泛的宁多鲁斯，本书详细介绍的是最常遭遇到的那些，见@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia.JournalEntryPage.21nindoru0000000]{此处}。

作为游戏中相对较新的内容，玩家们可能不熟悉宁多鲁斯——这很好！发现这种新类型的邪魔，是肆季鬼志核心谜团的重要组成部分。身为善解的信徒的玩家角色可能会知道一些关于它们的事，如@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog18sangpo.JournalEntryPage.18nindorus000000]{此处}所述。任何玩家角色都不应在开始这条冒险路径时就受训于宁多鲁学识，但一旦他们在第一幕接近结尾时或第二幕初期得知这些邪魔的存在，你就应当让玩家们知道，他们的玩家角色可以选择这一项，甚至可以鼓励其中一些人利用这场战役中大量的休整模式时间，重训为这项特别实用的学识。

About Nindorus

While a wider range of nindorus certainly exist, this book details those the most commonly encountered @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog21bestia.JournalEntryPage.21nindoru0000000]{Here}.

As relatively new additions to the game, players might not be familiar with nindorus—this is good! The discovery of this new type of fiend is a big part of Season of Ghosts’ central mystery. A PC who is a follower of Sangpotshi might know something about them, as detailed @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog18sangpo.JournalEntryPage.18nindorus000000]{Here}. No PC should begin this Adventure Path trained in Nindoru Lore, but once they learn about these fiends near the end of Act 1 or early in Act 2, you should let the players know this is an option for their PCs and perhaps even encourage some to take advantage of this campaign’s copious amounts of downtime to retrain into this particularly useful Lore.

Society.name: 社群 Society
Society.text:
社群

现存关于宁多鲁社会结构的大多数信息都相当零散。 诅咒之地的恶魔，幽灵和妖怪 一书由来自神门的匿名幽冥典狱官与来自紫霞的轮回裔共同撰写，包含了目前可得最详尽的资料。

根据这部著作，宁多鲁斯最常以小群体形式出现，但当足够多的它们聚集在同一片区域时，便会结成由十到五十个成员组成的游牧单位。这些群体通常由大量较弱的宁多鲁斯与少数更危险的变种领导者构成。这种群体被称为“灵煞”——是对“灵那萨提”一词的讹变；后者是轮回裔语中表示“家人”的古词。尽管名字如此，其中却几乎没有许多宁多鲁群体中常见的照料与情谊。相反，灵煞强调传播腐化、衰败、失落与毁灭。

灵煞的构成会经常变化，因为成员会离开队伍去追随各自的强迫冲动，或寻找新的狩猎场。灵煞也会在那些邪魔罕见地陷入内斗时发生变动，而内斗通常源于对猎物的争执。虽然宁多鲁不会犹豫杀死自己的同类，但它无法从这种猎杀中获取滋养，因此大多数宁多鲁都会把狂暴留给更美味的灵魂。

宁多鲁斯对凡人的信仰或神祇的事务几乎毫无兴趣，不过侍奉少数已知宁多鲁半神之一的那些个体则是显著的例外（这些存在也被称为@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog19cycles.JournalEntryPage.19nindoruascet00]{灵堕魔苦行者}）。宁多鲁斯通常无视其他神祇的作为，但有两个例外。它们对@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.aTYy1WHwAZiuei4h]{月夜尊}——月之主宰、@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.6O4UGWcYERDEugzk]{同时也越发崇拜文业王}复生的兄弟——以及@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QZD0u1jxwz0kj8uI]{法莱斯玛}怀有格外恶毒的蔑视。饰有月夜尊翡翠之月的圣祠，或受法莱斯玛螺旋徽记庇护的墓地，常会被单个宁多鲁或整个灵煞看中并占作领地；它们从以血腥屠戮亵渎这些区域中获得扭曲的快感。

说到那些同样嗜好杀戮的相似邪魔，宁多鲁斯对合作毫无兴趣，几乎同样可能与恶魔、魔鬼或其他邪魔发生争斗。不过，那些自称以宇宙为领域的存在——例如罗刹——有时会发现自己处于可能寻求与宁多鲁斯结盟的位置。尽管如此，宁多鲁斯仍能容忍与其他生物合作，尤其是在对方愿意以大量灵魂作为报酬时。具有讽刺意味的是，人们也曾见过宁多鲁斯与亡灵一同行动——而亡灵正是最常被拿来与它们混淆的生物类型。在这些合作关系中，宁多鲁斯通常充当首领，指挥食尸鬼、僵尸吸血鬼，或将无心智亡灵当作可供寄宿的躯壳，进而把它们改造成亡灵与宁多鲁生命交融而成的怪异混合体。

Society

Most of the information that exists on nindoru social structure is fragmented. Demons, Ghosts and Yokai of the Cursed Lands , a tome penned by anonymous Gloom Wardens from Shenmen and samsarans from Zi Ha, contains the most detailed information available at the moment.

According to this text, nindorus are most often encountered in small groups, but when enough of them gather in a single region, they band together in nomadic units ranging from ten to fifty. These groups are typically made up of a large number of less powerful nindorus led by a few of the more dangerous variants. This grouping is known as a “ninsat”—a mangling of “ninashsati,” an archaic samsaran term for “family.” Despite the name, there is little in the way of the care and camaraderie found in many nindoru groups. Instead, ninsats emphasize spreading corruption, decay, loss, and ruin.

The makeup of ninsats changes on a regular basis as members wander off to follow their own compulsions or seek fresh hunting grounds. Ninsats also shift during the rare occasions that the fiends fall into infighting, usually caused by disputes over prey. While a nindoru won’t hesitate to murder its kin, it’s unable to take nourishment from such kills, so most choose to save their rage for more delicious souls.

Nindorus have little interest in the faiths of mortals or the affairs of the gods, although those who serve some of the few known nindoru demigods (known also as @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog19cycles.JournalEntryPage.19nindoruascet00]{Nindoru Ascetics}) are notable exceptions. Nindorus tend to ignore the works of other deities, with two exceptions. They feel particularly vicious contempt for @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.aTYy1WHwAZiuei4h]{Tsukiyo}, lord of the moon and the resurrected brother of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.6O4UGWcYERDEugzk]{Fumeiyoshi}, as well as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QZD0u1jxwz0kj8uI]{Pharasma}. Shrines emblazoned with Tsukiyo’s jade moon or graveyards protected by Pharasma’s spiral are often sought out as territories by a nindoru or entire ninsats, who derive perverse pleasure from desecrating such areas with carnage.

When it comes to similar fiends with a shared appetite for bloodshed, nindorus have no interest in cooperation and are as likely to fight against demons, devils, or other fiends. Those who call the Universe their domain, though, such as rakshasas, sometimes find themselves in positions where they might seek an alliance with nindorus. Regardless, nindorus can tolerate cooperation with other creatures, especially if offered a bountiful supply of souls as payment. Ironically, nindorus have also been seen alongside undead, the creature type they are most often confused with. In these partnerships, nindorus usually act as leaders commanding ghouls, jiang-shi vampires, or using mindless undead as husks to inhabit and transform into strange amalgamations of undeath and nindoru life.

Ecology.name: 生态 Ecology
Ecology.text:
生态

宁多鲁斯存在于自然法则之外，然而它们依然存在于自然世界之中——与大多数邪魔不同，它们所关联的是宇宙本身，而非浩瀚众界中的另一处位面。尽管它们本身并不天然遵循生态系统的法则，却会被驱使去以某种方式扰乱环境，而这几乎会让它们落入一种近似的生态角色——哪怕那似乎完全是一种自我毁灭的角色。每一种宁多鲁都体现了某一特定循环的断裂，除此之外，也体现了造就它们的生死循环的普遍破裂。

宁多鲁斯会被驱使去吞食灵魂，但只有那些在桑博齐的往复洪流中漂流过多次的灵魂，才接近足以满足它们的饥渴。宁多鲁理想中的灵魂，是那种已经转生数次、且当前活着时仍保有前世记忆（无论部分还是全部）的灵魂。对宁多鲁而言，一个浸润了多世共同经验与感知的灵魂，就像一瓶陈放得恰到好处的美酒。

若将这一病态的比喻再推进一步，可以想象宁多鲁斯拥有近似侍酒师分辨葡萄酒原料的技能。它们能够直觉判断一个灵魂是否转生过。从宁多鲁斯手中幸存并活下来的人，常常会报告说，这些恶魔曾对所谓的前世说出令人不安地私密的话语。大多数人永远无法验证这些说法是真是假，因为回忆前世的能力是只有少数人拥有的赋礼。具志坚吉一是首位在《开拓者编年史》中发表宁多鲁详细记述的人；他说，那邪魔告诉他，他的灵魂“呈现出古老血渍的颜色”，并且曾寄宿于一名战士的身体之中；那名战士在八桥之战中被刀刃将头劈成两半而死。尽管这一说法无从证实，但它仍深深震撼了吉一。

宁多鲁会在身体死亡时吞食灵魂，在形而上意义上于灵魂离开被杀死的血肉之际将其“撕碎”，使那灵魂更难被带回——无论是回归生命，还是转为亡灵。这样的灵魂并不会被阻止继续前往来世或再次转生，因为宁多鲁斯仅吞食其中一部分灵魂能量；但那些在遭受这种袭击后重返生命的人，往往会过上更为艰辛的生活，并经历一些会让他们觉得自己仿佛受到了诅咒、注定不幸，或只是单纯倒霉的事情。那些在被宁多鲁斯吞食后又转生的、格外愤懑的灵魂，若在途中找不到开悟，甚至可能会选择自己也作为宁多鲁斯归来。

所有宁多鲁斯都拥有将思想化作实体之物的能力，不过它们之中最弱小者仅能显现武器、护甲或工具。更强大的宁多鲁斯能够显现生物、改变环境，或显现情绪与记忆，而非实体物体。这些显现无论本质为何，外观总是衰败、破损且令人不适——然而当被创造它们的存在使用时，它们的功效却与完整之物一样好，甚至更好。有人报告过这种力量一种格外令人不安的变体：当人们在战斗中面对宁多鲁时，会目睹它们从那人自己的过去中显现出破损的武器、工具，甚至是人，然后再用那个物体或生物来对付他们。这种情绪操纵是某些更强大宁多鲁斯所采用的策略；它们可能会显现一件童年时最喜爱的玩具、早已逝去父母的模糊影像，或爱人的戒指。宁多鲁会利用这种显现为自己取得优势，同时一点点侵蚀对手的决心。

Ecology

Nindorus exist outside the laws of nature, yet they still exist within the natural world–unlike most fiends, their association is with the Universe itself, rather than another plane of the Great Beyond. While they themselves do not intrinsically obey the laws of an ecosystem, they are compelled to disrupt environments in a way that almost results in the same sort of role—if only a role that seems entirely self-destructive. Each type of nindoru epitomizes the fracture of a specific cycle in addition to the generalized fracturing of the life and death cycle that created them.

Nindorus are compelled to feast on souls, but only souls who have drifted through the recurrent stream of Sangpotshi multiple times come close to satisfying their hunger. A nindoru’s ideal soul is one that has reincarnated several times and is currently living a life while having memories (either partial or full) of previous lives. To a nindoru, a soul imbued with the collective experience and wisdom of multiple lives is like a fine wine allowed to age just right.

To take this morbid analogy further, one can imagine that nindorus possess the equivalent of a sommelier’s skill at discerning a wine’s ingredients. They can intuit whether a soul has been reincarnated or not. Those who have survived encounters with nindorus often report that the demons made disturbingly intimate statements about so-called past lives. Most will never be able to verify whether or not these statements were true, as the ability to recall past lives is a gift few possess. Gushiken Giichi, the first to publish a detailed account of a nindoru in the Pathfinder Chronicles, said the fiend told him his soul “was the color of an ancient bloodstain” and had once been housed in the body of a warrior who died during the Battle of Eight Bridges after a blade cleaved his head in two. While impossible to confirm, the claim still shook Giichi to his core.

The nindoru feeds on a soul upon the death of its body, metaphysically “shredding” the soul as it exits the slain flesh and rendering it difficult for that soul to be returned—either to life or undeath. These souls are not prevented from traveling on to the afterlife or being reincarnated, for nindorus feed on only a fraction of that soul’s energy, but those who come back to life after suffering such an attack often live harsher lives and experience things that might make them feel cursed, doomed, or simply unlucky. Particularly bitter souls reincarnated after being devoured by nindorus might even choose to return as nindorus themselves if they can’t find enlightenment along the way.

All nindorus have the ability to manifest physical things from their thoughts, although the least powerful of their kind are limited to the manifestation of weapons, armor, or tools. More powerful nindorus can manifest creatures, alter their environments, or manifest emotions or memories instead of physical objects. These manifestations, regardless of their nature, always appear decrepit, broken, and unpleasant—yet when used by their creators they function as well, if not better, than they would if they were whole. Some report a particularly unnerving variant of this power, in which those facing a nindoru in battle witness them manifesting broken weapons, tools, or even people from the person’s own past, only to use that object or creature against them. This emotional manipulation is a stratagem used by some of the more powerful nindorus; they might manifest a favorite childhood toy, faded image of a long-deceased parent, or a loved one’s ring. The nindoru uses this manifestation to its advantage while simultaneously eroding its foe’s resolve.

Appearance.name: 外观 Appearance
Appearance.text:
外观

各种不同类型的宁多鲁斯有着千差万别的形态，但它们全都共有某些特征。大多数宁多鲁斯都带有模糊的人形轮廓，并且常因其消瘦的躯体、破损或错位的肢体，以及类似伤口的特征而被误认为是不死生物。不了解情况的人常常以为宁多鲁斯与食尸鬼有关，而龙华生物学家出版的一部天夏典籍《帝国的亵渎者》中，甚至错误地将这些生物认定为“异常的丧尸变种”。宁多鲁的影响确实能让像丧尸这样无心智的不死生物变成更加骇人的形态，这无疑助长了这种误解。事实上，这种混淆或许正是多年来缺乏恰当宁多鲁研究的原因之一；所幸如今人们正开始纠正这一危险的疏忽。

仔细观察宁多鲁斯，会发现许多完全属于它们自身的特征。即便是形态最怪异的个体，其外形中通常也会融入某种类人特征——无论是在本不该长出手臂的地方生出手臂，还是在身体某个藏匿部位，例如喉咙深处，露出一张隐约可辨、带着狞笑的脸。宁多鲁斯往往显得双眼失明、受损，甚至完全缺失，却依然能看得一清二楚，这表明那些已经挣脱灵魂轮回的生物不可能真正拥有这类器官。

无论呈现何种形态，宁多鲁的身体都反映着毁灭的本质，并象征着它们打破生死循环的角色。它们的手臂与双腿往往显得痛苦地拉长、折断或脱位，但仍保有与健康凡人肢体同等、甚至更强的力量与敏捷。它们的血肉常显得蜡黄、腐朽，甚至像是受了致命重创。这些特征正是许多人将宁多鲁斯误认为不死生物的主要原因，但它们其实确实是活着的——它们那超自然的身体并不受生物学与健康法则的束缚。其他一些宁多鲁斯则可能完全缺失某个本应存在的身体部位，例如胸腔，甚至整个头；而这些部位往往会被柳条笼子、摇曳的提灯，或其他通常并无生命的物体所取代。

当宁多鲁穿戴衣物或使用武器、工具时，它们总是偏好那些破损、失去光泽，甚至彻底毁坏的饰品与器具。大多数使用武器的宁多鲁斯所挥使的都是破损的武装，而它们的超自然本质会使这些武器变成魔法。被它们那错位的手掌挥舞时，这些武器能够造成可怕的创伤；但一旦脱手，便会崩解为尘埃。

宁多鲁斯由那些彻底抛弃轮回转生或死后存在这一概念的灵魂直接形成，且一出现便已完全成熟。最危险、最强大的宁多鲁斯，往往源自堕落的桑钵或背弃生死循环的轮回裔之灵魂；但没有任何灵魂会“意外”成为宁多鲁。抛弃循环、让自身不朽灵魂暴露于这等命运之下的选择，通常发生于参与复杂仪式的过程中，以确保其灵魂挣脱世界；而且这种决定必须始终在活着时出于自由意志作出（尽管欺瞒与诡计也可能诱使某些可悲之人在未理解全部后果的情况下作出这一选择）。

许多宁多鲁斯还共有一个怪异特征：令人毛骨悚然的血红色蝴蝶会聚集在宁多鲁身体中的空洞空间里，或仿佛自其血肉中完整地爬出。对许多人而言，蝴蝶象征着转变与变化；然而，从未有人见过与宁多鲁相关的毛虫，这暗示这些“灵堕魔蝴蝶”比表面看上去更加不同寻常。有人认为，灵堕魔蝴蝶是宁多鲁破碎灵魂的显现；也有人相信，它们是宁多鲁逸散思绪的化身。这些蝴蝶在离开其邪恶宿主后通常不会存活太久，最终会消散成红色烟雾，或化作墙壁与地板上的血渍般痕迹。

Appearance

The various types of nindorus have a wide variety of forms, yet all of them share certain features in common. The majority have vaguely humanoid shapes and are often mistaken for undead due to their emaciated frames, broken or disjointed limbs, and wound-like features. The uninitiated often assume that nindorus are related to ghouls, and an entry on the creatures in Defilers of the Empire, a Tian text published by Lung Wa biologists, incorrectly identified nindorus as “unusual zombie variants.” The fact that nindoru influence can empower mindless undead like zombies into even more horrific shapes and forms certainly doesn’t help with this misconception. In fact, this confusion may have contributed to the lack of proper nindoru research over the years, a dangerous oversight that’s thankfully now being rectified.

A close inspection of nindorus reveals many characteristics that are entirely their own. Even those with the most bizarre forms usually incorporate some humanoid feature in their shape, be it the growth of arms where no arms should be or the presence of a vaguely face leering from a hidden part of the body, such as the depths of the throat. Nindorus often seem to have blinded, damaged, or entirely missing eyes, yet see with perfect clarity, displaying how creatures who have broken away from the cycle of souls can’t possess such organs.

Regardless of the shape they take, a nindoru’s body reflects the nature of destruction and symbolizes their role in breaking the cycle of life and death. Arms and legs often appear painfully elongated, broken, or dislocated, yet retain as much (if not more) strength and agility as healthy mortal limbs. Flesh often appears sallow, decaying, or even grievously wounded. These features are the primary reason many mistake nindorus for undead, yet they are very much alive—their supernatural bodies not being bound to the laws of biology and health. Other nindorus might be entirely missing an expected part of the body, such as the chest or even the entire head—often replacing such body parts with wicker cages, flickering lanterns, or other normally inanimate objects.

When a nindoru dresses or uses weapons or tools, they invariably prefer accessories and devices that are broken, tarnished, or outright destroyed. Most nindorus who use weapons wield broken armaments that their supernatural nature empowers to become magical. When brandished in their disjointed hands, these weapons can inflict grievous wounds, but upon being released, they crumble into dust.

Nindorus form fully grown from souls who have abandoned the very concept of reincarnation or life after death. The most dangerous and powerful nindorus tend to rise from the souls of fallen Sangpots or samsarans who have turned their back on the cycle of life and death, but no soul can “accidentally” become a nindoru. The choice to abandon the cycle and expose one’s immortal soul to such a fate often occurs through participation in complex rituals to ensure their soul breaks free from the world, and it must always be made freely while alive (although deception and trickery can delude tragic figures into making this choice without realizing the full ramifications).

One strange element shared by many nindorus are the eerie blood-red butterflies that gather in the hollow spaces in a nindoru’s body or seem to crawl, fully formed, from their flesh. To many, the butterfly is a symbol of transformation and change, yet no caterpillar has ever been seen in association with a nindoru, suggesting that these “butterflies” are something more than they appear. Some suggest that nindoru butterflies are a physical manifestation of the nindoru’s broken soul, while others believe them to be incarnations of the nindoru’s stray thoughts. These butterflies rarely live long after fluttering away from their fiendish host, fading into red smoke or bloodstain-like markings on the wall or floor.

Cycles of Destruction.name: 毁灭轮回 Cycles of Destruction
Cycles of Destruction.text:
毁灭轮回

与大多数邪魔不同，后者的起源可追溯至时间深处，甚至往往早于凡俗生命这一概念本身；宁多鲁斯则是宇宙舞台上相对新近的来客。然而，随着时间推移，他们的存在却可能扩散到现实的所有角落。

历史文献表明，第一批宁多鲁斯诞生于三千多年前天夏自仪兴帝国极盛之时。在那个时代，一名人类孩童出生于轮回裔父母之家，却在不久后被送交给一个人类社群抚养，因为他的生父母希望儿子能过上和谐的人生，并在下一次生命轮回中转生术为轮回裔之身。然而，这个孩子后来长成了一名愤怒的青年，名叫西格克，并因父母遗弃自己而怨恨他们。成年后，他找到了亲生父母；可当他发现他们甚至都不是人类时，他心中的苦毒迅速扩大，转而指向所有轮回裔，尤其是那些追随桑博齐者。西格克质问，为何开悟只能通过死亡与重生的缓慢术过程达成，而业力却像某种武断的裁判，决定着灵魂的命运。

随着年岁渐长，西格克开始痴迷于在桑博齐轮回之外达成完美。他拜许多强大的施法者为师，最终长期侍奉于一名名叫宁多鲁的巫妖门下。那巫妖向这名易受影响的年轻人灌输不死的种种可能，告诉他那是一种完美状态，能够在不把经验与感知牺牲给转生术那种漫长反复的摆布下实现。西格克对此深感兴趣，却认定灵魂笼子会成为自己无法承受的弱点。经过五年研究后，西格克背叛了宁多鲁并摧毁了这名巫妖，随后偷走前导师的灵魂笼子加以实验，并将巫妖的灵魂困在其中多年。在这些年里，西格克聚集了大批志同道合的学者，以及那些拒绝桑博齐教诲的人；同时也越发崇拜文业王——天夏掌管坟墓的庇护者。帝国纪年4444年，西格克率领他规模庞大的会众举行了一场亵渎神明的仪式，意图强行让被困的宁多鲁灵魂转生术为某种新事物，某种游离于既有生死轮回之外的存在。西格克许诺，这将会“粉碎音波桑博齐之轮，将我们所有人从转生术的笼子中解放出来。”

关于西格克计划举行这场仪式的记录至今仍然存在，也有文献记载了他在选定执行该秘仪日期之前的人生经历。但在那命定之日后，有关西格克、他的实验以及其教团的一切便都无从查找了。他和追随者仿佛只是凭空消失，如同被逐出了现实本身。然而，就在同一年稍后，最早关于灵堕魔的记载开始出现，而大多数人都认为这两起事件在时间上的重合绝非巧合。数个世纪以来，人们一直相信，西格克以某种方式成功将自己的祈求者转化为最初的宁多鲁斯，而这些邪魔随后又杀死了他们的创造者。但近期证据揭示了灵堕魔半神的存在，其中甚至有一位就以西格克为名——这或许意味着，那名心灰意冷的人类是通过将自己化为自身毁灭的化身，获得了一种扭曲版本的开悟。

当然，宁多鲁斯中最强大的那些个体却持有不同看法，因为他们声称自己一直都存在于创世造物之外，直到西格克的行动才终于让他们得以进入这现实轮回——而这些邪魔如今则宣称，这将是最后一个轮回，因为当他们得偿所愿时，世上将只剩下宁多鲁斯。

Cycles of Destruction

Unlike most fiends, whose origins date back to the depths of time and often predate the very concept of mortal life itself, nindorus are a relatively new arrival on the cosmic stage. In time, however, their presence could potentially spread throughout all corners of reality.

Historical documents suggest that the first nindorus came into being during the height of Tian Xia’s Yixing empire over three thousand years ago. In that era, a human child was born to samsaran parents only to be given over to a human community shortly thereafter, as his birth parents hoped their son would live a harmonious existence and reincarnate into a samsaran body during his next life cycle. Instead, this child grew into an angry youth named Sigek who resented his parents for abandoning him. He sought them out as a young adult, but upon discovering his parents weren’t even human, his bitterness swiftly bloomed to encompass all samsarans, especially those who followed Sangpotshi. Sigek demanded to know why enlightenment was only achievable via a slow process of death and rebirth, with karma serving as an arbitrary judge of a soul’s fate.

As he matured, Sigek became obsessed with achieving perfection outside the cycle of Sangpotshi. He apprenticed himself to a host of powerful spellcasters, eventually entering into a lasting servitude under a lich named Nindoru. The lich filled the impressionable young man’s mind with the possibilities of undeath, telling him it was a perfect state that could be achieved without sacrificing experience and wisdom to the laborious whims of reincarnation. Sigek was intrigued, but concluded that a soul cage would be a vulnerability he could not afford. After five years of study, Sigek betrayed Nindoru and destroyed the lich, then stole his former master’s soul cage for experimentation, keeping the lich’s soul trapped within its cage for years. Over those years, Sigek gathered a sizable following of like-minded scholars and those who rejected the teachings of Sangpotshi while increasingly venerating @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.6O4UGWcYERDEugzk]{Fumeiyoshi}, Tian Xia’s patron of graves. In 4444 ic, Sigek led his sizable congregation in a blasphemous ritual intended to force Nindoru’s trapped soul to reincarnate into something new, something outside of the established cycle of life and death. This, Sigek promised, would “Shatter the wheel of Sangpotshi and free us all from the cage of reincarnation.”

Records of Sigek’s plans to perform the ritual still exist, as well as documents chronicling his life before the date he chose to perform the rite. But after that fateful day, nothing can be found about Sigek, his experiments, or his cult. He and his followers seemed to have simply vanished, as if cast out of reality itself. Yet later that same year, the first accounts of nindoru fiends began to appear, and most agree that the timing of these two events is no coincidence. For centuries, it was believed that Sigek somehow managed to transform his supplicants into the first nindorus, and the fiends subsequently murdered their creator. But recent evidence has revealed the existence of nindoru demigods, including one bearing the name Sigek—perhaps a sign that the disillusioned human achieved a twisted version of enlightenment by transforming himself into an incarnation of his own destruction.

The most powerful of the nindorus themselves, of course, hold different beliefs, for they claim to have always existed beyond the creation of creation itself, and it was only Sigek’s actions that finally allowed them into this cycle of reality—a cycle that the fiends now promise will be the last, for when they have had their way, only the nindorus will remain.

Reincarnation Ancestry Feats

While few remember their previous lives, save for those who have been reincarnated via ritual, any who have lived lives before their current one carry within their soul the weight of previous existences. When one does recall those previous lives, one can draw upon memory and experience in a way most ancestries can’t. Whatever the circumstances, your new lease on life has expanded your mind thanks to the bits and pieces you recall of your soul’s past adventures.

Major Spirit Powers

These spirit powers tap further into the heroes’ undead-adjacent state, giving them the abilities of ghosts and other spirits. These abilities can be extremely potent in the hands of PCs and allow for creative solutions to standard adventuring problems. Since major spirit powers are about granting more significant ghost-themed abilities and aren’t associated with emotions and personality traits, players shouldn’t run into thematic disconnects when choosing a major spirit power, but just as with minor spirit ones, you should feel free to change names and themes as you see fit to give your players more appealing choices for them to make.

下等魂力

Haunting the Living.name: 萦扰生者 Haunting the Living
Haunting the Living.text:
萦扰生者

引用给GM的注释

此处呈现的魂力并非设计用于第10章之外的游戏——它们会赋予玩家角色超出其正常能力范围的额外力量，因此不应在该章之外的游戏中使用。出自 《开拓者：亡者之书》的 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.52nzskpmUt9AjUf8]{Ghost} 变体，是想要允许幽灵玩家角色进行长期游戏时的绝佳选择。

当玩家角色在第三幕期间转生到现世时，他们会显现为受困于生与不死之间某处的存在。处于这一状态时，玩家角色大体上行动如常，但会呈现为自身半凝实的灵浆版本。他们并非完全透明，但其坚实的身体边缘会显得摇曳闪烁，带来一种怪异而令人不安的外观。处于这一状态时，他们是活体生物，但会获得下列部分与不死生物共享的类似能力。作为更接近魅影的活体生物，他们依然会受到虚无伤害影响，并由活力效果治疗。

不死视觉：他们获得微光视觉；如果其族裔已经拥有微光视觉，则改为获得黑暗视觉。

转生求生：处于这一状态的玩家角色永远不会获得受伤（状态），但在从濒死（状态）恢复时会改为暴露于灵魂劣化（见下文）。如果玩家角色在转生期间死亡，他们会在柳岸镇心景中苏醒，保持活着，并获得 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} 状态。

转生防护：他们对抗疾病、毒素、睡眠术，以及任何会施加麻痹（状态）的效果时，其豁免骰（或任何其他防御）获得+2环境加值。

魂力：处于这一状态时，玩家角色可以通过他们新获得的魂力与现世互动。当玩家角色在现世显现其转生之躯时，他们各自从后续页面列出的魂力中获得两个下等魂力和一个上等魂力。每当玩家角色进行每日准备时，他们都可以重新选择已选的魂力。当魂力要求进行豁免骰时，使用该玩家角色的职业DC或法术DC中较高者。任何要求攻击掷骰的魂力，使用此DC – 10。决定任何反制检定的效果时，使用该玩家角色自身的等级。

灵魂劣化：起初，玩家角色很可能会沉醉于他们新获得的魂力之中。然而，每当一名转生中的玩家角色接近死亡时，他们都要冒着彻底迷失于自身幽灵本性的风险。每次一名处于濒死的转生玩家角色本应正常获得受伤（状态）时，他们会改为暴露于灵魂劣化，并且必须尝试一次新的豁免骰，以抵抗这一诅咒阶段的提升。

灵魂劣化 诅咒 7

  • 罕见
  • 诅咒
  • 魔法

玩家角色的自我感会被幽灵般的欲望吞没，最终使其变成一具没有意识的空壳。灵魂劣化不会随着时间流逝而提升或降低其阶段。取而代之的是，每当一名转生中的玩家角色从濒死（状态）恢复时，他们都必须针对这一诅咒尝试一次新的豁免骰。玩家角色在第10章中可能遭遇的某些事件或效果，也会迫使他们对灵魂劣化进行豁免。一旦某位玩家角色身上的转生仪式效果结束，他们会立刻并完全从灵魂劣化中恢复。

Haunting the Living

A Note For GMs

The spirit powers presented here aren’t intended for play outside of Chapter 10—they grant additional powers to PCs beyond their normal capabilities and shouldn’t be used in play beyond that chapter. The @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.52nzskpmUt9AjUf8]{Ghost} archetype from Pathfinder Book of the Dead is an excellent option for longer-term games where you want to allow ghostly PCs.

When the PCs transmigrate into the living world during Act 3, they manifest as beings trapped somewhere between life and undeath. While in this state, the PCs function mostly normally but appear as semisolid ectoplasmic versions of themselves. They aren’t quite transparent, but their solid bodies seem to waver and shimmer along the edges, giving them an eerie, unsettling appearance. While in this state, they’re living creatures but gain some of the following abilities similar to those shared by undead creatures. As living creatures more akin to phantoms, they remain susceptible to void damage and are healed by vitality effects.

Undead Vision: They gain low-light vision, or darkvision if their ancestry already has low-light vision.

Transmigrated Survival: A PC in this state never gains the wounded condition but instead becomes exposed to soul degradation upon recovering from the dying condition (see below). If a PC dies while transmigrated, they awaken, alive, in the Willowshore mindscape and gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} condition.

Transmigrated Protection: They gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws (or any other defense) against disease, poison, sleep, and any effects that would impose the paralyzed condition.

Spirit Powers: While in this state, the PCs can interact with the living world via their newfound spirit powers. When the PCs manifest their transmigrated bodies in the living world, they each gain two minor spirit powers and one major spirit power from the spirit powers listed on the following pages. Every time the PCs do their daily preparations, they can reselect their chosen spirit powers. When a spirit power calls for a saving throw, use the higher of that PC’s class DC or spell DC. Any spirit powers calling for attack rolls use this DC – 10. Use the PC’s own level for determining the effects of any counteract checks.

Soul Degradation: Initially, PCs will likely revel in their newfound spirit powers. Whenever a transmigrated PC comes close to death, however, they risk losing themselves entirely to their ghostly nature. Each time a dying transmigrated PC would normally gain the wounded condition, they’re instead exposed to soul degradation and must attempt a new saving throw to resist increasing the stage of this curse.

Soul Degradation Curse 7

  • rare
  • Curse
  • magical

The PC’s sense of self becomes subsumed by ghostly desires, eventually rendering them a senseless shell. Soul degradation doesn’t increase or decrease its stage over the passage of time. Instead, each time a transmigrated PC recovers from the dying condition, they must attempt a new saving throw against this curse. Certain events or effects that the PCs might encounter in Chapter 10 can also force them to save against soul degradation. Once the effects of transmigrate ritual end for a PC, they immediately and fully recover from soul degradation.

  • Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:23|traits:curse,magical];
  • Stage 1 spirit weakness 5;
  • Stage 2 spirit weakness 10;
  • Stage 3 spirit weakness 10, and each time the PC critically fails an attack roll or skill check, they’re @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} as their mind obsesses over the failure;
  • Stage 4 as stage 3;
  • Stage 5 as stage 3;
  • Stage 6 The PC is reduced to an unthinking haunt. Until the curse is removed or the duration of the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.8Lk9K3tRnV68MQPW]{Transmigrate} ritual ends, they repeat a short loop of actions and are no longer under the control of the player (unlimited duration).

The following six spells are said to have been originally created by Zhi Hui, founder of the Tan Sugi monastery. In truth, the spells predate Zhi Hui, and their use was merely advocated by her in life. Even though she lacked the skill to cast all six of these spells, she made a point of preserving their knowledge and making them available to her followers. In this adventure, they exist only in the form of six fragile scrolls hidden away in a secret room in the Tan Sugi monastery ruins.

Heroic Legacies

The following rare magic items were once used by heroic figures in Tian Xia’s past. The mysterious merchant Shinzo managed to gather working replicas of these four items, and he offers them as gifts to the PCs at the start of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2apsog11faceto]{Chapter 9}. You can have Shinzo relate these legends to the PCs as he gives them the items, or you can allow the PCs a chance to recall these stories of heroic deeds and legendary accomplishments themselves by succeeding at a @Check[society|dc:26|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check or a logically associated Lore check to Recall Knowledge. Magic Tea.name: 魔茶 Magic Tea
Magic Tea.text:
魔茶

特殊的原料、独特的冲泡方法，以及魔法强化，会将普通的茶转变为可消耗的物品，并提供额外增益。在第2幕中，玩家角色们取悦柳岸镇的神使后，会获得本节中详述的全部魔茶配方作为奖励。

茶（特征）：魔茶是一种药水。它会在你饮用时启动，并因此被消耗掉。魔茶具有药水和茶特征。当你制作一剂魔茶时，你所提供的原料会以稀有且昂贵的茶叶形式体现。制作魔茶的过程包括将魔法试剂注入茶叶、净化水质，并将茶叶浸泡于水中，最终制成的本质上是一种格外美味的药水。你可以在饮用魔茶或将其喂给另一生物时，以一个交互行动来启动它，如同药水一般。你也可以用一个需要10分钟的行动来启动魔茶，此行动需要纯银茶具（这套工匠工具包最多可由四名同时进行此行动的人共用）来备茶，然后在一场简短的茶道中将其饮下或奉给他人，之后魔茶的效果便会开始；以这种方式启动魔茶会强化其效果，具体如以下各物品“茶道”条目所述。

一旦你饮下一剂魔茶，在接下来的24小时内，你会暂时免疫该种特定类型的魔茶。

Magic Tea

Special ingredients, unique brewing methods, and magical enhancements transform common teas into consumable items that provide additional benefits. The PCs are rewarded with the formulas for all of the magic tea detailed in this section after they entertain Willowshore’s kami in Act 2.

Tea (trait): Magic tea is a type of potion. It activates when you drink it, which uses it up. Magic tea has the potion and tea traits. When you craft a dose of magic tea, the raw materials you supply are in the form of unusual and costly tea leaves. The process of crafting magic tea includes infusing the leaves with magical reagents, purifying the water, and steeping the tea in the water, resulting in what’s essentially a particularly delicious potion. You can activate magic tea with an Interact action as you drink it or feed it to another creature, as if it were a potion. You can also activate magic tea with a 10-minute activity that requires sterling tea ware (this artisan’s toolkit can be shared by up to four people who take this activity simultaneously) to prepare the tea and then consume it or present it to someone during a short tea ceremony, after which the magic tea’s effects begin; activating magic tea in this way enhances its effect, as detailed in each item’s Tea Ceremony entry below.

Once you drink a dose of magic tea, you’re temporarily immune to that particular type of magic tea for 24 hours.

Bestiary and NPCs.name: 怪物图鉴与非玩家角色 Bestiary and NPCs

Zhi Hui.name: 智惠 Zhi Hui
Zhi Hui.text:
智惠 善良的寺庙幽灵

在智惠来到后来成为丹杉寺的地方之前，她曾作为流浪者生活在幽魂之森的精魂之间。很久以前，一个如今早已被遗忘的小村庄的村民为了平息愤怒的精魂，将她遗弃在那里。智惠并未屈服于怪物，反而被神使发现并抚养长大。她遵循他们的指引，在15岁时便获得了开悟，随后独自踏上探索幽魂之森的旅程。多年后，她听闻一片杉树林的传说：那里的杉树高耸于森林其余树木之上，树干大得如同整间茅屋。智惠不禁疑惑，杉树为何能生长到如此极端的程度，于是动身寻找那片林地。她又花了三年才找到那些树木，因为幽魂之森的这片区域既荒野又未曾探索；但即使她当时还不知道其意义为何，她也明白自己来到了一处具有重大意义的地方。

当智惠最初建立丹杉寺与柳岸镇时，她只是希望创造一个地方，让桑博齐的弟子能够将一生奉献于追求开悟。那片杉树林让她心生敬畏，她发现高度集中的灵性能量会导致这些树木异常高大。她很快揭开了这片林地的阴暗秘密——一个巨大的邪恶沉眠于其根系之下，唯有一位英雄灵魂转生为林中最高大的树木后所具备的灵性抗力，才能阻止那邪恶从死亡中逃脱。发现此事后，她穷尽自己所能运用的资源，并联络遍及天夏的友人，最终查明了那邪恶的本质。名为苦迦菩提的一位宁多鲁半神被埋葬在大杉树之下，而她也因此献身于守护这些杉树；正是这些树木反过来保护着所有村民，使他们免受那邪魔侵害。

智惠大师去世后，她的灵魂起初仍与寺院相系，以监督对那片林地的防护；但随着她的追随者离去或堕落，她的灵魂也同样落入了苦迦菩提的掌控之中。如今，她已几乎无法阻止正在展开并将导致可怕局势的事件：苦迦菩提的苏醒。

战役角色

当玩家角色在寺院中净化圣像时，智惠能够回答他们更多的问题，并对他们施放法术；一旦四尊圣像全部被净化，她便能随意施放法术、回答问题，甚至还能在战斗中提供协助——只要战斗发生在包含已净化圣像的遭遇区域之一。玩家角色可能向智惠提出的一些问题，其回答如下。

苦迦菩提是谁／是什么？“苦迦菩提是一名宁多鲁邪魔，其存在与桑博齐的哲学背道而驰。将近一千年前，他被谭隋靖击败。她也在战斗中死去，但她的灵魂转生为一棵高耸的杉树，生长在苦迦菩提的遗骸之上，作为封印将他的灵魂困住。这座寺院中央的杉树，正是那一棵树。但它已经恶心了，因为苦迦菩提正努力寻求重生。他的影响正是你们一直面对的那些可怖怪异之物的根源。这座寺院曾是一处神圣之地，武僧们在此照料土地、动物与精魂。同时，甚至在寺院建立之前，这里就是一处将苦迦菩提那庞大邪恶封印于地表之下的地点。我本希望这座寺院能够世世代代守望苦迦菩提之墓，但我没有预见到我自己的死亡会如何影响我的追随者。没有人准备好接替我的位置。更糟的是，我的一名学生，辛月，已被苦迦菩提腐化，甚至即便现在？仍在他墓穴下方劳作，意图让那邪魔的灵魂重获新生。如今，聚集于此的邪魔们一直在亵渎散布于寺院各处的圣像，以增强苦迦菩提的影响。”

关于折磨柳岸镇的诅咒，你能告诉我们什么？“这座寺院建在这片神圣的树林中，但我当时并不知道，大杉树封印着一名强大而邪恶的邪魔，名叫苦迦菩提。正是这名邪魔的影响，导致了眼下正在展开的悲剧。困住你们与柳岸镇的并非寻常诅咒，而是你们的时代本身被偷走了。我们全都被困在一个循环往复的心景之中，它每年重复一次，从夏日第一天开始，到春天最后一天结束。每当循环重启，你们的记忆也会被重置。我保有自己的记忆，但我不知道这个循环已经重复了多少次；而且直到现在，我都无法看穿苦迦菩提的黑暗。不过，我知道是谁开启了这一切——你们的总督，赫山宝。他试图增强丹杉，但它本不需要增强。他的尝试适得其反，在苦迦菩提之墓上打开了裂缝——那些裂缝将我们所有人都拖入了这个循环的心景之中。那甚至足以把赫山宝从这个困住我们其余人的心景中卷走。虽然我无法说出我们重复这个循环多少年了，但我知道这一次有些事情改变了——无论是由于苦迦菩提日益增长的力量，还是其他外部力量所致。重要的是，你们已经得到了改变我们命运的机会；如果你们想解放我们所有人，就绝不能浪费这个机会。要阻止循环，你们必须揭开事情真相，而第一步就是终结苦迦菩提对这个心景的影响。”

我们要如何脱身？“我不知道你们所寻求的答案。如果有谁知道，那一定是赫山宝。是他造成了这一切，但他现在被困在了自己的心景之中。一旦苦迦菩提的影响被削弱，你们就会发现可供追寻的小路与可供搜索的线索，它们必定会引导你们找到总督的去向。找到赫山宝，你们就会更接近理解如今究竟发生了什么，以及如何从这个恶意循环中脱身。”

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.season-of-ghosts-bestiary.Actor.uFg1TnTBpXNYGF9o]{智惠} 生物 7

  • 独特
  • 中型
  • 幽灵
  • 虚体

Zhi Hui Benevolent Monastic Ghost

Before Zhi Hui arrived at what would become the Tan Sugi monastery, she lived as a nomad among the spirits of the Specterwood after being abandoned there to appease angry spirits by the villagers of a small, now long-forgotten village. Rather than succumb to monsters, Zhi Hui was instead discovered and raised by kami. She followed their guidance and achieved enlightenment at the age of 15 before setting out on her own to explore Specterwood. Years later, she heard the story of a grove of sugi trees that towered over the rest of the forest, with trunks as large as entire huts. Wondering how sugi trees could grow to such extremes, Zhi Hui set out to find the grove. It took her three more years to find the trees, for this part of Specterwood was wild and unexplored, but she knew she’d come across a place of immense significance even if she didn’t yet know what it meant.

When Zhi Hui initially founded both the Tan Sugi monastery and Willowshore, she’d simply hoped to create a place where disciples of Sangpotshi could dedicate their lives to the pursuit enlightenment. The sugi grove instilled a sense of awe in her, and she discovered that a high concentration of spiritual energy caused the trees to grow abnormally large. She soon uncovered the grove’s sinister secret—that a great evil slumbered beneath its roots and only the spiritual resistance of a heroic soul who’d reincarnated as the tallest tree in the grove kept that evil from escaping its death. Following this discovery, she scoured the resources available to her and reached out to friends throughout Tian Xia before finally determining the nature of the evil. A nindoru demigod named Kugaptee was buried beneath the Great Sugi, and she dedicated herself to protecting the sugi trees that in turn protected all of the villagers from the fiend.

After Master Zhi Hui’s passing, her spirit initially remained tied to the monastery to oversee the protection of the grove, but as her followers left or became corrupted, her spirit became trapped in Kugaptee’s clutches as well. Now, she can do little to stop the events that unfold and are leading to a dire situation: Kugaptee’s awakening.

Campaign Role

As the PCs purify statues in the monastery, Zhi Hui can answer more of their questions and cast spells on them; once all four statues are purified, she can cast spells and answer questions at will and can even aid in combat as long as the fight takes place in one of the encounter areas that contains a purified statue. Certain questions the PCs might ask Zhi Hui are answered as follows.

Who/What is Kugaptee? “Kugaptee is a nindoru fiend whose existence stands in opposition to the philosophy of Sangpotshi. Nearly a thousand years ago, he was defeated by Tan Sui-Jing. She perished in the fight as well, but her soul reincarnated as a towering sugi tree that grew over Kugaptee’s remains, serving as a seal that would keep his soul trapped. The central sugi tree in this monastery is that very tree. But it has sickened, for Kugaptee strives for rebirth. His influence is the source of the monstrosities you’ve been facing. This monastery was once a sacred place, with monks who cared for the land, the animals, and the spirits. At the same time, and even before the monastery, it has been a site that kept Kugaptee’s immense evil sealed away beneath the surface. I had hoped that this monastery would stand guard over Kugaptee’s grave for many generations to come, but I failed to see how my own death would affect my followers. No one was ready to take my place. Worse, one of my students, Xin Yue, became corrupted by Kugaptee and even now toils below in his grave to see the fiend’s soul reborn. Now, the fiends who have gathered here have been desecrating the statues scattered throughout the monastery to amplify Kugaptee’s influence.”

What can you tell us of the curse that afflicts Willowshore? “This monastery was built in this sacred grove of trees, but unknown to me at the time, the Great Sugi seals away a powerful and evil fiend named Kugaptee. It is this fiend’s influence that has caused the tragedy unfolding now. It is no mere curse that traps you and Willowshore. Time itself has been stolen from you. We are all trapped in a cycling mindscape that repeats every year, beginning on the first day of summer and ending on the last day of spring. Each time the cycle repeats, your memories have been reset. I retain my memories, but I know not how often the cycle has repeated and, until now, have not been able to see further than Kugaptee’s darkness. But I know who started it—your governor, Heh Shan-Bao. He sought to bolster the Tan Sugi, but it needed no bolstering. His attempt backfired and opened cracks into Kugaptee’s grave—cracks that plunged us all into this cyclic mindscape. It was enough to whisk Heh Shan-Bao away even from this mindscape that traps the rest of us. While I cannot say how many years we’ve repeated this cycle, I do know that something has changed this time—whether due to Kugaptee’s growing strength or other outside forces. What is important is that you have been given the chance to change our fates, and you must not waste this opportunity if you wish to free us all. To stop the cycle, you must uncover the truth of what happened, and that begins with ending Kugaptee’s influence over this mindscape.”

How can we escape? “I do not know the answer you seek. If anyone does, it would be Heh Shan-Bao. He caused all of this, but he is now trapped within his own mindscape. Once Kugaptee’s influence has been diminished, there will be trails to follow and clues to seek that will surely lead you to where your governor has gone. Find Heh Shan-Bao, and you will get closer to understanding what is happening now and how to escape from this cycle of malice.”

Xin Yue.name: 辛月 Xin Yue
Xin Yue.text:
辛月 苦迦菩提祭司

辛月记得自己所有的前世。起初，她将这种能力视为神祇的恩赐，让她能在每次死亡并转生后，运用自己积累的知识来改善人生境遇。虽然她略微偏好转生成女性，因为那更符合她最初的身体，但她也很快学会享受以男性之身度过的人生。归根结底，对辛月而言，只要灵魂仍然完整，身体的实际形态并不重要。

作为桑博齐的信徒，她每一世都在不断接近开悟。她与一些长寿的精魂结为朋友，而这些精魂总是很高兴她以最新的身体前来拜访。随着一世世人生延续下去，她最终获得了开悟。也正是在本应是她最后一次转生之时，她来到丹杉寺，并引起了苦迦菩提的注意。当智惠去世时，苦迦菩提被困于丹杉之下的死亡之中，但在辛月悲痛最深之际，祂悄然将自己的影响渗入了她的梦境。在接下来那可怕的数月里，宁多鲁对辛月的影响日益加深。在这些梦中，辛月与苦迦菩提越来越频繁地就转生的价值展开激烈辩论，而随着时间推移，这种腐化最终发展到辛月将自己献给这位宁多鲁半神——她已将其视为那位“让她看清开悟虚妄”的主宰。

之后，辛月将注意力转向寺院中所剩无几的武僧，并开始引诱他们改信苦迦菩提。然而，直到辛月在其他武僧眼前将自己献作祭品给那邪魔——随后又转生进她如今的身体——他们才也一并皈依。对他们而言，辛月揭示了丹杉寺并非一处和平之地，而是一座笼墓；若他们能释放其中被囚禁的囚徒，便可立刻获得强大的力量与奖励，而不是苦苦等待无数次转生，只为博取某种他们甚至可能永远无法得到的机会。

辛月现在的身体是一名身材矮小的人类女性，有着齐肩短发，以及一条垂至小腿的黑色长辫。她总是以愉快的态度、脸上带着和善笑容说出可怕的话语，以此在追随者心中激起畏惧与敬重。她那永恒不变的礼貌并非伪装，即便在威胁他人、许诺惩罚时也是如此。即使以尽可能漫长且痛苦的方式屠宰受害者，她也会对他们微笑，并真诚地感谢他们的牺牲。

当赫山宝的仪式杀死柳岸镇的人民，并将这片地区拖入心景时，辛月和她的武僧也一同死去了。然而，他们并没有在心景中重返生命。由于他们与苦迦菩提的亲近与奉献，他们未能复生，并在过去115年的每一次循环中都以不死生物的形态存在。对辛月而言，这具新身体是可耻而可怖的负担；她只希望，通过帮助苦迦菩提实现祂的欲望——将祂昔日仇敌肉身的化身，也就是如今生长在祂坟墓之上的杉树，作为构筑一具崭新活体的原始材料——她自己也能重生为新的形态。她对自己将获得什么样的身体兴趣不大，只在乎那必须是一具活生生的血肉之躯。

战役角色

辛月一手促成了丹杉寺的覆灭与苦迦菩提的苏醒，自那以后，她便一直为祂的复活而努力。和英雄们一样，辛月在过去115年里也一直被困于心景之中；但由于她与苦迦菩提之间的联系，她保留了每一次循环流逝的记忆。她一直在关注柳岸镇的镇民，但在经历了一个世纪、一次次打破自身循环的失败后，她已不再将他们视为会妨碍自己工作的威胁。因此，当她收到苦迦菩提的异象，看到玩家角色们打开幽魂之墙时，她确实大吃一惊。

尽管辛月外表近乎骷髅、呈现不死生物的模样，她仍旧保持着自己的礼貌；她丝毫不掩饰自己的意图。她对英雄们并无私人的怨念。虽然她表面上可能显得通情达理，但只要苦迦菩提的存在仍留在心景之中，就没人能说服她放弃自己的追求；为了实现目标，她会战斗到最后一刻。

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.season-of-ghosts-bestiary.Actor.ExTKQvgLI72XGk98]{辛月} 生物 7

  • 独特
  • 中型
  • 不死生物

Xin Yue Priestess of Kugaptee

Xin Yue remembers all of their previous lives. They originally saw this ability as a blessing from the gods that allowed them to use their accumulated knowledge to better their station in life each time they died and were reincarnated. While they slightly preferred being reincarnated as a woman, because it matched their first body, they quickly grew to enjoy their lives in a man’s body as well. Ultimately, to Xin Yue, the actual form of their body was unimportant as long as their soul remained whole.

As a follower of Sangpotshi, each lifetime they lived saw them growing ever-nearer to enlightenment. They befriended long-lived spirits who were always happy for them to visit in their latest body. As their lives continued on, they eventually attained enlightenment. It was during what would’ve been her final reincarnation that she came to the Tan Sugi monastery and drew Kugaptee’s attention. Though trapped in death below the Tan Sugi when Zhi Hui passed away, Kugaptee crept his influence into Xin Yue’s dreams when her grief was most profound. Over the awful months to follow, the nindoru’s influence over Xin Yue grew. In these dreams, Xin Yue and Kugaptee increasingly engaged in lively debates over the value of reincarnation, and over time, this corruption grew to the point that Xin Yue dedicated herself to the nindoru demigod, whom she had come to consider as the Lord who “opened her eyes to the frivolity of enlightenment.”

Xin Yue then turned her attention to the few remaining monks at the monastery and began to lure them over to the worship of Kugaptee. However, it wasn’t until Xin Yue offered herself as a sacrifice to the fiend before the other monks’ eyes—only to be reincarnated into her current body—that they converted as well. To them, Xin Yue had revealed that the Tan Sugi monastery wasn’t a place for peace, but a cage-tomb that, if they could release its bound prisoner, would grant great power and rewards immediately, rather than waiting for countless reincarnations for a chance at something they might never even earn.

Xin Yue’s current body has the form of a human woman with a short build, shoulder-length cropped hair and a long black braid that hangs to her calves. She strikes fearful respect into her followers by saying terrible things with a cheery attitude and a kind smile on her face. Her perpetual politeness isn’t a facade, even as she threatens and promises punishment. While butchering her victims in the most prolonged and painful way possible, she smiles at them and earnestly thanks them for their sacrifice.

When Governor Heh Shan-Bao’s ritual slew the people of Willowshore and plunged the region into a mindscape, Xin Yue and her monks perished as well. However, they didn’t return to life within the mindscape. Their proximity and devotion to Kugaptee kept them from life, and they’ve spent each cycle of the past 115 years as undead. To Xin Yue, this new body is a shameful and horrific burden, and she only hopes that by helping Kugaptee to achieve what he desires—using the incarnation of his old enemy’s body, now the sugi tree that grows over his grave, as the raw building blocks of a new living body—that she too shall be reborn into a new form. She has little interest in what kind of body she might attain, just that it be one of living flesh.

Campaign Role

Xin Yue fabricated the circumstances for the Tan Sugi monastery to fall and for Kugaptee to awaken, and she’s been working toward his revival ever since. Like the heroes, Xin Yue has been trapped in the mindscape for the past 115 years, but due to her connection with Kugaptee, she retained the memories of each passing cycle. She’s kept tabs on the townsfolk of Willowshore, but after a century of repeated failures to break their own cycle, she discounted them as a threat to her work. As such, she was truly surprised when she received a vision from Kugaptee that showed the PCs opening the Wall of Ghosts.

Despite her nearly skeletal, undead appearance, Xin Yue continues to foster her politeness; she doesn’t hide her intent in any way. She has no personal grudge against the heroes. Although she might come across as reasonable, as long as Kugaptee’s presence remains within the mindscape, she can’t be reasoned with to stop her pursuits and fights to the bitter end to achieve her goal.

Ren Mei Li.name: 任美璃 Ren Mei Li
Ren Mei Li.text:
任美璃 柳岸镇络新妇公主

任美璃是一位耐心而狡猾的谋划者，决心扩大自己在神门的势力范围。她培养不走寻常路的代理人与手段，最终着眼于阴司察夕的王座。

任美璃出生于宫城阴司察夕，自睁眼起便沉浸在络新妇低语交织的阴谋之中。然而，在成年后不久，她便对姐妹们的行事方式感到幻灭，主要是因为那妨碍了她沉溺于自己偏爱的享受。预言破灭之年伊始，络新妇宫廷夺取了神门的控制权，当时的任美璃和她的姐妹一样残酷而善于操纵人心，但岁月最终改变了这些特质。

虽然让惊恐的臣民宣誓服从、建立自己的宫廷影响力的确自有其吸引力，但任美璃真正热爱的却是表演。无论是黑风岸烟火、皮影戏、剑丝舞剧，还是天夏各地上演的种种戏剧艺术，都令她心醉。她常伪装成人类女子，离开神门，游历大陆各地，只为观看最精妙的演出；但每当她试图劝说自己最钟爱的表演者前来神门，为她和她的姐妹献艺时，对方往往都会拒绝。他们告诉她，再多银钱也不值得让自己在那片闹鬼的土地上冒生命危险，而且他们也无法相信这个国家的络新妇统治者会保障他们的安全，却始终没有意识到，自己正在交谈的女子本身就是一位络新妇。

任美璃并未采取防备姿态，反而从他们的角度思考这个问题，并很快得出结论：那些表演者的顾虑是有道理的。神门确实危险，而太多络新妇也并不可靠。正是在她愿意理解这种视角的过程中，她意识到这里存在一个巩固自己权力基础的巨大机会。

任美璃的新哲学很简单：只要她信守自己作出的每一个承诺，人们就会明白她是可以依靠的。只要她不替其他络新妇作出任何承诺，并且明确表示自己并不代表其余同类发言，那么她赢得的信任就只会归于任美璃本人。这样的安排既能强化追随者对她的忠诚，也能确保他们不信任她的竞争对手。

如果她审慎治理，投入资源改善基础事务，并避免对臣民施加过度残酷的压迫，那么她的领地就会变得更加高产而有利可图，使她能把更多财富挥霍在自己喜爱的奢华享受上。感激之情会增强民众的忠诚，使她的对手更难动摇她的地位，也能减少诸如匪患之类源于饥饿与混乱的问题。久而久之，也许表演者们对前来神门分享其艺术的邀请便不会再如此犹疑。

经过数十年的艰苦工作，任美璃已经建立起一张值得信赖的代理人与使节网络。她挑选代表时，首先看重的是能力——这在神门相当罕见——而在大多数情况下，他们也都忠心效力。这份忠诚是双向的：任美璃会迅速保护自己的资产，因为她明白，整个网络的力量都建立在代理人相信她也会为他们竭力而为的基础上。

虽然她的一些仆役是理想主义者，但任美璃本人并非如此。她是个以自利为先的务实之人，追求善政是因为这对她有利，而不是因为她真的在乎自己的人民。对于自己领地之外的任何臣民，她都无意改善其处境，因为在她看来，自己表面上的仁慈与神门其他地方那些络新妇反复无常的残酷之间的鲜明对比，正是她最关键的优势之一。

不过，她也发现，装作并非如此很有用。任美璃最终且深藏不露的目标，是从琅蕾夫人手中夺取阴司察夕的丝绸王座。公开场合中，她否认自己怀有这样的野心，但暗地里，这早已是她多年来的终局目标。为实现这一点，她已在本地农民、野心勃勃的商人以及外国使节之间铺垫舆论，让他们将她登位的前景视为极可能为神门带来一个开明统治的黄金时代。若她的派系果真崛起掌权，这些闪耀的梦想或许甚至真的会成真——至少会在任美璃觉得它们有用的范围内如此。

战役角色

任美璃是玩家角色在第12章中的关键盟友，也可能是他们在神门更长远野心中的重要助力。尽管她的动机是自私的，但她的行动往往会使她的人民受益。任美璃本性与其统治实际效果之间的这种反差，可能会为某些团队带来有趣的问题与两难。不过，应当明确的是，无论她出于什么理由采取这些政策，它们确实为困在这片险恶土地上的普通人创造了一处相对安全的避风港。

在这场冒险中，任美璃不会在战斗中与玩家角色并肩作战——同样地，如果他们愚蠢到向她发起战斗挑战，她也会尽力避免造成持久伤害，而是使用自己的魔法，通过 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.vLA0q0WOK2YPuJs6]{魅惑术} 和 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.qwlh6aDgi86U3Q7H]{暗示术} 来尝试平息敌意。若这些手段失败，她便会使用 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.VlNcjmYyu95vOUe8]{传送} 或白银雾行来撤退，给玩家角色时间冷静下来，之后再通过中间人，或彻底伪装成另一个人，与他们重新接触。

Ren Mei Li Jorogumo Princess of Willowshore

A patient and cunning schemer, Ren Mei Li is determined to increase her sphere of influence in Shenmen. She cultivates unorthodox agents and approaches with an eye, ultimately, toward claiming the throne of Yin-Sichasi.

Born in the palace-city of Yin-Sichasi, Ren Mei Li was immersed in the whispering intrigues of the jorogumo from the time she opened her eyes. Soon after reaching her majority, however, she became disillusioned with her sisters’ ways, chiefly because it impeded her ability to indulge her preferred tastes. When the jorogumo court seized control of Shenmen at the onset of the Age of Lost Omens, Ren Mei Li was as cruel and manipulative as her sisters, but time would see these traits change.

While securing obeisance from terrified subjects and building her courtly influence did have a certain appeal, Ren Mei Li’s true love was performances. Be they Hei Fengan fireworks, shadow puppet plays, sword-and-silk dance operas, or any of the theatrical arts displayed across Tian Xia, they all delighted her. Disguised as a human woman, she traveled beyond Shenmen and across the continent to attend the finest shows, but more often than not, when she tried to coax her favorite performers to visit Shenmen and perform for her sisters, they refused. No price in silver was worth risking their lives in that haunted land, they told her, and they couldn’t trust the country’s jorogumo rulers to keep them safe, never realizing the woman who they spoke to was a jorogumo herself.

Rather than respond defensively, Ren Mei Li considered the problem from their point of view and soon concluded that the performers’ qualms were justified. Shenmen was dangerous, and so many jorogumo were unreliable. In her willingness to understand this perspective, she realized there was a great opportunity to strengthen her base of power.

Ren Mei Li’s new philosophy was simple: if she honored all her promises, then people would learn that she could be relied on. If she refrained from promising anything on behalf of other jorogumo, and indeed made it clear that she didn’t speak for the rest of her kind, then the trust she would earn would be limited to Ren Mei Li personally. This arrangement would both bolster her loyalists’ allegiances and ensure they distrusted her rivals.

If she governed prudently, invested in basic improvements, and refrained from excessive cruelty to her subjects, then her fiefdom would become more productive and profitable, enabling her to spend even more lavishly on the luxuries she loved. Gratitude would strengthen her people’s loyalty, making it more difficult for her rivals to undermine her and reducing problems, such as banditry, that stemmed from hunger and disorder. And in time, perhaps performers wouldn’t be so hesitant toward invitations to share their art in Shenmen.

After decades of intensive work, Ren Mei Li has developed a trusted network of agents and delegates. Her representatives are chosen for ability above all, a rarity in Shenmen, and for the most part, they serve faithfully. This loyalty runs both ways: Ren Mei Li is quick to protect her assets, knowing that the strength of her entire network depends on her agents believing she’ll exert similar efforts on their behalf.

While some of her servants are idealists, Ren Mei Li herself isn’t. She’s a self-interested pragmatist who pursues good governance because it benefits her, not because she particularly cares about her people. Ren Mei Li has no interest in improving the lot of any subject outside her own domain since she considers the contrast between her seeming benevolence and the capricious cruelty of the other jorogumo elsewhere in Shenmen to be one of her key advantages.

However, she’s found it useful to pretend otherwise. Ren Mei Li’s ultimate, deeply hidden goal is to seize the silken throne of Yin-Sichasi from Lady Lang Loi. Publicly, she denies any such ambition, but it’s secretly been her endgame for years. To achieve this end, she’s laid groundwork among local peasants, ambitious traders, and foreign envoys to view the prospect of her ascension as likely to usher in a golden age of enlightened rule in Shenmen. Should her faction rise to ascendance, these starry dreams might possibly even come true, at least to the extent that Ren Mei Li finds them useful.

Campaign Role

Ren Mei Li is a key ally for the PCs in Chapter 12, and potentially for their longer-term ambitions in Shenmen. Although her motivations are selfish, her actions tend to benefit her people. This dichotomy between Ren Mei Li’s nature and the actual effect of her rule might present interesting questions and dilemmas for some groups. However, it should be clear that whatever her reasons for adopting them, her policies do create a comparative safe haven for ordinary people trapped in a treacherous land.

In this adventure, Ren Mei Li doesn’t fight alongside the PCs in battle—likewise, if they foolishly challenge her to combat, she’ll do her best to avoid doing lasting harm, instead using her magic to try to defuse the hostilities using @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.vLA0q0WOK2YPuJs6]{Charm} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.qwlh6aDgi86U3Q7H]{Suggestion}. If these fail, she’ll use @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.VlNcjmYyu95vOUe8]{Translocate} or Silver Mistwalk to retreat and give the PCs time to calm down, after which she’ll attempt to engage with them again via intermediaries or while disguised as a different person entirely.
